item.title: iPhone, Tk5,000 debt, older friends and TikTok lure: What led to Apratim’s murder?
item.description:
What initially appeared to be the murder of a 13-year-old schoolboy for an expensive iPhone has developed into a more complex investigation involving a Tk5,000 debt, his association with older youths and TikTok videos used to lure him from home.
Police say Ishayat Shahriar Apratim was taken to a secluded part of Lalmai Hill in Comilla on Friday, assaulted and killed before his mother’s iPhone 17 Pro Max was taken. But investigators are now examining whether personal grievances also contributed to the killing.
Three people, including Saiful Islam Tuhin and two teenagers, have been arrested in the murder case filed by Apratim’s father, KM Firoz Shahriar.
Police are investigating whether another youth was involved.
The emerging picture is of a seventh-grader who had developed friendships with people several years older than him -- relationships involving motorcycle rides, photographs and TikTok videos -- before allegedly being lured to the isolated hills by people he knew.
Investigators say text messages were central to getting Apratim out of his home.
Tuhin repeatedly messaged him on Friday, asking him to come outside.
At one stage, Apratim was told they could use his expensive phone to shoot TikTok videos and take photographs, according to sources close to the investigation.
Apratim eventually agreed and left home with his mother’s iPhone at around 2:30pm. His family had understood that he was going out to take photographs with friends.
He never returned.
Police say Apratim met Tuhin shortly after 3pm. Their subsequent movements were captured by at least four CCTV cameras.
Footage showed Apratim and Tuhin walking and talking normally. Two other individuals were seen following them in one clip, while another showed all four together.
Their destination was a wooded area in Sananda in the Lalmai Hills, reached through an unpaved road about 1.5 kilometres from the main highway.
Police believe two other teenagers later joined Apratim and Tuhin there.
According to the initial police investigation, the group tried to take Apratim’s phone sometime between 5pm and 6pm.
When he resisted, a scuffle broke out. Police allege Tuhin struck him on the head with a bamboo stick before others also assaulted him.
After Apratim died, the group allegedly took the iPhone and fled.
Investigators are separately examining the role of another youth, Siam. Police information so far indicates he was not at the actual killing site, but investigators are checking whether he acted as a lookout nearby.
Apratim suffered a severe head injury, while other wounds were also found on his body. Investigators believe some injuries may have occurred after death when jackals dragged the body. Autopsy and forensic evidence is being examined.
The investigation has also uncovered another possible motive.
One of the arrested teenagers had worked at YesTech, a mobile-phone parts business owned by Apratim’s father.
Investigators learned that Apratim had lent him Tk5,000 and had recently begun asking for repayment.
Sources familiar with the interrogation said the teenager had become annoyed over the repeated demands and allegedly thought that if Apratim were no longer alive, he would not have to repay the money.
Police are examining the allegation as part of the motive.
Police detained Tuhin at around 9am on Saturday, before investigators knew Apratim was dead. His body was found later that day.
Investigators say Tuhin initially denied involvement but admitted his role after prolonged questioning.
He was initially reluctant to identify others, allegedly saying he had promised not to disclose their names.
During the interrogation, however, Tuhin’s phone repeatedly received calls from the teenager who worked at Apratim’s father’s company.
Police subsequently detained that teenager. Investigators say Tuhin then identified another teenager, who was also taken into custody.
Investigators are examining whether one suspect deliberately left his mobile phone behind on the day of the killing to conceal his location.
Police have yet to reach a conclusion and are examining technical evidence.
Police say the stolen iPhone ultimately led them to another crucial piece of evidence.
Investigators went to Tuhin’s home on Saturday evening, where his mother, Shirina Akhtar, retrieved the phone from underneath a mattress.
Family members told investigators that Tuhin had returned home before evening on Friday and asked his younger brother to hide the phone.
Apratim was a seventh-grade student at Border Guard Public School. School authorities described him as quiet, sociable and a good student with no known record of trouble.
But investigators are examining his social circle outside school.
Police found that those with whom Apratim associated were not his classmates and were older than him.
Investigators also found photographs and TikTok videos involving Apratim and the older youths.
His tutor, Al Amin, said Apratim was mature for his age and mixed easily with people of different ages, but tended to associate more with seniors.
The tutor said Tuhin would take Apratim to different places on his motorcycle, which may have helped deepen their friendship.
She had, however, noticed that Apratim had recently begun declining invitations to go out and had advised him to be careful about whom he associated with.
Apratim’s maternal uncle, Kazi Mahbubur Rahman, said the boy had come to know 19-year-old Tuhin through an older neighbourhood friend.
After Apratim disappeared, the family contacted Tuhin, who allegedly told them that although the two had planned to go out, Apratim ultimately had not joined him.
CCTV footage later showing the two together raised the family’s suspicions.
Police have not yet established a single definitive motive.
Investigators are now trying to determine how the planned theft of the iPhone, the Tk5,000 debt and the relationships between Apratim and the older youths intersected in the killing.
Forensic and technical evidence is also being analysed to establish the roles of each suspect.
Apratim’s mother, Nahida Begum, an associate professor at Comilla University, has raised additional suspicions, including whether earlier disputes involving local youths could have played a role.
Police have not established a connection between those issues and the killing.

IMF: 36% of educated youth in Bangladesh unemployed
item.description:
Thirty-six percent of educated young people in Bangladesh are unemployed, according to a report by the International Monetary Fund (IMF). The report, published in the September issue of the IMF’s Finance & Development magazine, said youth unemployment is high across Asia, with the highest rates recorded among more highly educated young people.
The IMF said artificial intelligence (AI) could boost economic growth and productivity. However, if AI adoption outpaces skills development, the technology could put additional pressure on young workers in the labour market.
The report also highlighted educated youth unemployment rates in several Asian countries, including India, Sri Lanka, Indonesia, Vietnam, Thailand, Singapore and the Philippines.
Fahim Mashroor, founder and managing director of Bdjobs.com, one of Bangladesh’s leading online job platforms, said that the number of bachelor’s degree holders has increased significantly over the past two decades.
In 2010, only 3.9% of the labour force held bachelor’s degrees. By 2022, the figure had risen to 9%, more than doubling in 12 years.
However, the job market has changed little, while the country’s economic structure has also remained largely unchanged. New industries have not emerged at a pace sufficient to absorb the growing number of graduates, Mashroor said.
According to him, around 2.2–2.3 million young people enter Bangladesh’s labour market each year, including about 750,000 university graduates.
The Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics’ (BBS) 2024 Labour Force Survey found 2.624 million unemployed people in the country, including 2.032 million aged 15–29. Nearly 29% of the unemployed were highly educated or held bachelor’s degrees.
BBS data also show that more than 17% of highly educated young jobseekers remain unemployed for over two years, while more than 15% remain unemployed for one to two years. In other words, roughly one in three highly educated young people remains unemployed for more than a year.
According to the IMF report, 43% of educated youth in Sri Lanka are unemployed, while the rate in India exceeds 40%. The rate is above 20% in Indonesia, Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia and the Philippines.
The IMF said highly educated young people are struggling to find jobs that match their qualifications. As AI use expands across Southeast Asian labour markets, concerns are growing that opportunities for highly skilled workers could decline in the coming years.
The issue, however, extends beyond unemployment figures, the IMF said. A persistent mismatch remains between the skills demanded by available jobs and those possessed by graduates.
With AI models now capable of performing many complex tasks at little or no cost, businesses may have less need for salaried entry-level technical positions, according to the IMF.
The IMF estimates that nearly 1.2 billion people will enter the labour force in developing economies over the next decade. More than half a century ago, around 500 million young people in emerging-market and developing economies were preparing to enter the workforce.
A World Bank report, The Global Jobs Challenge, published in June, said these young people are likely to constitute the largest youth group in history. Their numbers are expected to exceed those of any previous decade and surpass projections for every remaining decade of this century.

item.title: Fuel hikes threaten millions as living costs soar
item.description:
Millions across Bangladesh woke up to a grimmer economic reality on Monday (September 21), as the government implemented an aggressive across-the-board fuel price hike of Tk20 per litre.
Issued late Sunday night by the Ministry of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources, the decree pushes retail prices for diesel, kerosene, petrol, and octane to record highs.
Coming just five months after a Tk15 per litre jump in April, this secondary shock brings the cumulative increase in fuel prices to Tk35 per litre in less than half a year, dealing a heavy blow to households, agriculture, transportation, and industrial production nationwide.
The latest price adjustment sees diesel—the lifeblood of public transport, freight logistics, and irrigation pumps—soar from Tk115 to Tk135 per litre.
Petrol has jumped to Tk160 per litre from Tk140, octane to Tk165 from Tk145, and domestic kerosene to Tk155 from Tk135.
The fiscal dilemma
Explaining the price increase, state authorities pointed to intensifying Middle East conflict, shipping disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz, and soaring international crude and freight charges.
Between March and August, the Bangladesh Petroleum Corporation (BPC) accumulated a staggering loss of approximately Tk22,875.66 crore.
Without a retail price adjustment, BPC was losing nearly Tk89 per litre on diesel, creating a daily deficit of Tk109 crore and projected annual losses of Tk40,000 crore on diesel alone.
The government estimates the Tk20 increase will reduce BPC’s annual loss by roughly Tk10,000 crore, preserve foreign exchange reserves, and prevent cross-border smuggling into neighboring markets where prices remain comparatively high.
However, experts argue that transferring this fiscal burden onto the public will trigger severe knock-on effects across the broader economy.
Squeezing agriculture, logistics, and production
Diesel accounts for nearly two-thirds of all petroleum consumed in Bangladesh. The cascading effects of higher diesel prices will immediately spill into supply chains, expanding secondary inflation across every tier of commerce:
Transit operators and the Bangladesh Jatri Kalyan Samity warn that freight haulage and public transport fares must rise to cover fuel costs. Increased trucking rates will directly bump up retail shelf prices for raw agricultural produce and manufactured goods.
Exporters and industrial manufacturers, already grappling with severe industrial gas shortages, are relying heavily on diesel-powered back-up generators.
"Staying in business means staying competitive," noted Mohiuddin Rubel, additional managing director at Denim Expert Ltd. Rising energy overheads threaten to squeeze margins, erode export competitiveness, and force marginal enterprises to downsize.
Higher diesel costs mean heightened irrigation fees for farmers, driving up agricultural output expenses just as harvesting and planting cycles demand maximum power input.
Since low-income households spend the vast majority of their earnings on food and basic transport, even incremental fare or produce hikes severely compress real living standards.
The timing of the fuel hike coincides with severe humanitarian warnings. According to a country brief released by the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), roughly 18.1 million people in Bangladesh are projected to face high levels of acute food insecurity (IPC Phase 3 "Crisis" and above) between September and December 2026.
This reflects an 18% increase from the 15.3 million recorded between May and August, with nearly 787,000 individuals expected to reach IPC Phase 4 (Emergency) levels.
The FAO explicitly identified "constrained household purchasing power amid persistently high inflation, driven by elevated fuel and energy costs" alongside recent flood disruptions as the primary drivers eroding food access across vulnerable communities.
Compounding pressures on everyday survival
The fuel price shock does not exist in isolation; it compounds an array of ongoing cost-of-living pressures facing ordinary households:
Unequal safety nets
While approximately 1.4 million government employees are scheduled to receive wage increases starting October—partially shielding them from price surges—the vast majority of the national workforce enjoys no such cushion.
Over 85% of Bangladesh's labour force operates in the informal sector or within private industries where pay raises remain stagnant or non-existent.
For millions of rickshaw pullers, factory operatives, day laborers, and sales workers, real wages continue to fall.
Selim Raihan, executive director of Sanem and professor of economics at the University of Dhaka, emphasized that diesel is embedded in every layer of the macroeconomy.
"Once transport, irrigation, and distribution costs rise together, businesses and workers adjust expectations, making inflation far more persistent and harder to reverse," he noted.
Zahid Hussain, former lead economist at the World Bank's Dhaka office, stated that because fuel prices have risen in the international market, the government had no alternative but to raise domestic prices.
Compared to prices before the Iran war, the price of refined fuel has now increased by 43%. Keeping prices low would require the government to provide larger subsidies—a burden the government’s current fiscal capacity cannot support.
However, he noted that the policy of adjusting fuel prices at the beginning of the month was not followed, as prices were abruptly raised after the 20th of the month.
According to Hussain, higher fuel prices will inevitably drive up commodity prices in the market. However, care must be taken to ensure this does not lead to opportunistic profiteering under the guise of higher fuel costs.
He further observed that the government currently lacks the fiscal space to expand social safety net programs to help poor and low-income groups cope with this additional inflationary pressure. Therefore, the immediate priority must be to ensure that the benefits of existing programs effectively reach their intended beneficiaries.
SM Nazer Hossain, vice president of the Consumers Association of Bangladesh (CAB), noted that the announcement has created panic among the public because fuel prices are interconnected with almost every aspect of people's lives and livelihoods.
He added that a rise in fuel prices will increase costs everywhere—including industrial factories, offices, businesses, and households. When these expenses go up, the extra money ultimately comes out of the consumer's pocket, adding to the public's financial burden. At the same time, because fuel is linked to other goods and services, the prices of essential commodities could see another round of increases.
Navigating public discontent
Expressing regret over the decision, State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Anindya Islam Amit offered a sincere apology to the public.
He emphasized that the government was forced into an "unpopular decision" by external geopolitical shocks and rising import costs, assuring citizens that retail prices would be revised downward as soon as global oil markets stabilize.

item.title: Mariyam’s family alleges abuse, murder as MP Nazrul remanded
item.description:
The family of 19-year-old Mariyam Khatun, the second wife of Satkhira-4 MP Gazi Nazrul Islam, has alleged that she suffered months of physical and mental abuse at the lawmaker’s NAM Bhaban residence before being found hanging there on Sunday, with relatives now questioning whether her death was suicide.
Mariyam’s father, SM Masum Billah, filed a case accusing Nazrul, his first wife Maksuda Islam and Mariyam’s maternal uncle Obaidur Rahman of abetting her suicide.
Police arrested Nazrul and Maksuda, while Obaidur remains at large.
A Dhaka court on Monday placed Nazrul on four days’ remand and Maksuda on one day’s remand for questioning over the death.
But outside the Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College morgue on Monday, Mariyam’s grieving family went further, alleging she had been murdered and her body hung to make the death appear to be suicide.
No evidence establishing that allegation has yet been made public, and police are investigating the death.
Mariyam’s aunt, Shamsur Nahar Roksana, told Dhaka Tribune that she spoke with her niece almost every day and that Mariyam frequently cried while describing alleged verbal and physical abuse by Nazrul and Maksuda.
According to Roksana, Mariyam told her that life had become “unbearable”.
She alleged that both the MP and his first wife physically assaulted Mariyam.
“We suspect she was murdered and then hung,” Roksana said, naming Nazrul, Maksuda and Obaidur as those she believed responsible.
Mariyam’s uncle Mostasib made a similar allegation, claiming she had suffered physical and mental abuse before her death.
Her father, Masum Billah, said his daughter had carried “deep pain” and described the NAM Bhaban residence as “a prison for her”. He demanded a proper investigation and punishment for whoever was responsible.
The allegations of abuse also feature in the case filed by Mariyam’s father.
According to the FIR, Mariyam married Nazrul in June and subsequently lived with him and his first wife at Apartment 203 of NAM Building No 5, opposite the National Parliament.
Masum alleged that Mariyam had repeatedly told her family that Nazrul and Maksuda subjected her to physical and mental abuse following the marriage.
On Sunday at around 5:30pm, Nazrul called Masum and asked him to come to the apartment immediately, according to the case statement.
Masum arrived to find his daughter hanging inside the residence.
Police said the room had been locked from inside and was forced open, after which Mariyam was found hanging from a ceiling fan by her scarf. Investigators also recovered handwritten notes from her bed.
Police suspect the notes may have been written by Mariyam, but Tejgaon Division Deputy Commissioner Md Ibne Mizan said investigators would wait for a CID forensic examination before confirming the handwriting.
Masum said he could not confirm whether the notes were his daughter’s because he was unfamiliar with her handwriting.
The writings describe emotional distress, betrayal and anguish over sharing a husband.
One says the writer had trusted someone only to discover that person was on the “opposing” side of her struggle, while another reflects on loving a man who was already married.
Police produced Nazrul and Maksuda before Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Mohammad Ehsanul Islam on Monday, seeking seven days’ remand for both.
Investigating officer SI Shamsuzzoha Sarkar argued that the couple had been in the same residence when Mariyam died and that custodial interrogation was necessary to determine whether they had played any role in her death.
The defence opposed the request and sought bail, denying that either had any involvement.
After hearing both sides, the court granted four days’ remand for Nazrul and one day for Maksudah.
As he was leaving court, Nazrul rejected the allegations.
“The allegations brought against us are false. I was not at home at the time of the incident,” he told journalists.
Asked about Mariyam’s death, he said: “I know nothing about that.”
The Election Commission will act on the parliamentary seat of Nazrul, MP for Satkhira ‑ 4, only after receiving formal communication from the Speaker of the National Parliament, Senior Secretary Akhtar Ahmed said.
“We have not yet received any letter from the Speaker. Jamaat ‑ e ‑ Islami did inform us earlier that he had been expelled from the party,” Ahmed told reporters.
“The procedure dictates that the Parliament Secretariat must notify us. Our role is election management; subsequent steps fall under the Secretariat. Once the letter arrives, action will follow.”
Jamaat lawyer Shishir Monir reiterated the party’s position: “He is no longer associated with Jamaat. The State and Government of Bangladesh will take whatever action is required by law. Jamaat has no further statement.”

Fuel prices rise up to nearly 36% between January and September 2026
item.description:
Prices of all four major liquid fuels changed several times between January and September this year, with the latest hike of Tk 20 per litre taking effect from Monday.
With the latest revision, fuel prices have risen by up to nearly 36 percent from their January levels.
According to data from the Ministry of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources, diesel was sold at Tk 102 per litre in January this year, kerosene at Tk 114, petrol at Tk 118 and octane at Tk 122.
Under the latest rates effective Monday, prices have risen to Tk 135 per litre for diesel, Tk 155 for kerosene, Tk 160 for petrol and Tk 165 for octane.
Compared with January, diesel has increased by Tk 33 per litre, or 32.35 percent; kerosene by Tk 41, or 35.96 percent; petrol by Tk 42, or 35.59 percent; and octane by Tk 43, or 35.25 percent.
Kerosene recorded the highest percentage increase at 35.96 percent, while octane saw the largest increase in absolute terms at Tk 43 per litre.
Comparative historical data shows that in January 2024, fuel prices stood at Tk 109 per litre for diesel and kerosene, Tk 125 for petrol and Tk 130 for octane. By January 2025, prices stood at Tk 105 per litre for diesel and kerosene, Tk 122 for petrol and Tk 126 for octane.
At the beginning of the year in January, retail prices were set at Tk 102 per litre for diesel, Tk 114 for kerosene, Tk 118 for petrol and Tk 122 for octane.
Prices of all four fuels were reduced by Tk 2 per litre in February, bringing diesel to Tk 100, kerosene to Tk 112, petrol to Tk 116 and octane to Tk 120.
Fuel prices remained unchanged at the February rates until April 18.
Prices were raised from April 19, with diesel set at Tk 115 per litre, kerosene at Tk 130, petrol at Tk 135 and octane at Tk 140. The April 19 rates remained unchanged throughout the month of May.
Diesel remained unchanged at Tk 115 per litre, while kerosene, petrol and octane prices were increased by Tk 5 each, taking them to Tk 135, Tk 140 and Tk 145, respectively, in June. The June rates remained unchanged for July and August.
The government initially kept the August rates unchanged for September, but raised all four fuel prices by Tk 20 per litre from September 21.

item.title: Student alliance holds torch procession at DU demanding justice for Apratim, Azmul
item.description:
Gonotantrik Chhatra Jote held a torch procession and rally at the University of Dhaka on Monday, demanding the arrest and exemplary punishment of those involved in the killings of Comilla teenager Ishayat Shahriar Apratim and Khulna University student Md Azmul Hossain.
The organization also condemned the detention of 3 ninth-grade students in Dhaka’s Khilgaon and demanded their unconditional release.
The procession began from the university’s Teacher-Student Centre (TSC) at 7:30pm and passed through VC Chattar, Mall Chattar and Shadow before ending at the foot of the Raju Sculpture, where a brief rally was held.
At the rally, Tayub Islam, central office secretary of Biplobi Chhatra Moitri, said: “On one hand, people and children are being killed, while on the other hand, the state is showing extreme indifference. Bangladesh has now turned into a place of death. The sound of these deaths does not reach the Ministry of Home Affairs. They are constantly making indifferent remarks to us.”
He added: “We are living in a state where there is no guarantee of a natural death. Those who are repeatedly involved in killings, disappearances and terrorism are not being brought under the law. This culture of impunity is constantly pushing people’s lives towards crisis.”
Tayub Islam further said: “The state itself is committing crime. There is no discussion in parliament about people’s lives or the future of children; rather, terrorists are being patronized. We have to break this structure of oppression in the hands of the state. Without breaking this state, it is not possible to ensure our right to die a natural death and security of life.”
Shubhashish Chakma, vice-president of the Pahari Chhatra Parishad, said: “When we talk about the deterioration of the law-and-order situation, the home minister or the administration says that it is not possible for them to guard everyone’s bedroom. But we want to say that those carrying out acts of terrorism, abduction and looting are able to do so because they are being given the opportunity. Due to the culture of impunity, criminals are getting out through loopholes in the law.”
He added: “The state’s culture of impunity is directly responsible for this extreme decline in people’s human and moral values.”

Kabaddi team beat Taipei to boost Asian Games medal hope
item.description:
Bangladesh brightened their medal hopes in men’s kabaddi at the 20th Asian Games with a nerve-wrecking 48-47 points victory over Chinese Taipei in their second Group A match held on Monday at the Tokai Citizen Gymnasium in Nagoya, Japan.
Bangladesh led 24-20 at half-time after opening a seven-point advantage at one stage.
The match remained fiercely contested after the break, with both sides attacking aggressively and tempers occasionally flaring. Bangladesh held their nerve cool in the closing stages to secure their second straight victory.
Bangladesh bagged four lonas while Chinese Taipei collected two.
The victory puts Bangladesh in a strong position to reach the semifinals. A win over Japan in their third group match on Tuesday will secure a semifinal place and at least a bronze medal, with India awaiting them in their final group match.
Under kabaddi rules, all four semifinalists are guaranteed medals.
Bangladesh coach Abdul Jalil said defensive mistakes had made the match more difficult than expected but expressed confidence ahead of Tuesday’s clash with Japan.
Earlier on the day’s morning, Bangladesh beat South Korea by 39-35 points in their opening Group A match.

Taka strengthens against dollar after 5.5 years
item.description:
Ending a continuous depreciation trend spanning five and a half years, the Bangladeshi taka (BDT) has shown signs of appreciation against the US dollar, according to a Bangladesh Bank (BB) report released recently.
On a point-to-point basis from June last year to June this year, the value of the taka appreciated by 0.06%.
Furthermore, between August 30 and September 17, the local currency strengthened by 0.77% against the greenback.
Central bank data show that the Taka experienced an unbroken streak of depreciation against the US dollar from 2021 until September 17 this year.
During this period, the exchange rate surged from Tk85.80 per dollar to a record high of Tk123.95 -- reflecting a devaluation of Tk38.20, or 45.05%.
However, the trend began reversing in the second half of this year.
After peaking at Tk123.95 on August 30, the dollar rate dropped by Tk0.95 to Tk123.00 on September 17, resulting in a 0.77% gain for the taka over those three weeks.
The Bangladesh Bank report also compared regional currency movements from June last year to June this year.
The Indian rupee depreciated by nearly 9.5%, the Sri Lankan rupee lost over 10%, and the Indonesian rupiah declined by around 9%.
The Malaysian ringgit and Chinese yuan both gained nearly 4%, while the Pakistani rupee appreciated by around 2%.
The central bank noted that after a prolonged period of weakening, the Bangladeshi Taka has shifted to a relatively stronger position.
A depreciating Taka directly elevates import costs for fuel, industrial raw materials and food items, passing price increases on to consumers, driving inflation and dampening real purchasing power -- especially for low- and middle-income households. It also increases the domestic currency burden of servicing foreign debt.
Conversely, a strengthening Taka relieves pressure on import expenditures and lowers the local currency cost of foreign debt servicing, though the broader impact will depend on future trends in imports, exports, remittances, foreign exchange reserves and international market conditions.

item.title: Govt eases conditions to import synthetic fibres
item.description:
The government has brought a series of amendments to the Import Policy Order 2026–2029, relaxing several conditions for the readymade garments (RMG), textile, and industrial sectors.
In particular, opportunities have been expanded for importing fabrics used in producing high-value and specialized apparel made from synthetic fibres (man-made fibres).
Additionally, the rules for importing capital machinery for setting up industries have been simplified.
The Import and Internal Trade-1 Branch of the Ministry of Commerce issued a notification in this regard on Sunday (September 21).
These amendments were introduced under the powers conferred by the Imports and Exports (Control) Act, 1950, and the Import Policy Order 2026–2029. The notification comes into effect immediately.
According to the new amendments, specialized synthetic fabrics used in the production of seamless sportswear, high-value fashion goods, and functional apparel can now be imported regardless of size and shape.
However, a recommendation from the relevant garment sector association—BGMEA or BKMEA—will be required.
Furthermore, provisions have been clarified for importing raw materials and packaging materials against back-to-back LCs or contracts as per the Utilization Declaration (UD) or Utilization Permission (UP) for exporting specialized textile and hosiery products.
Items listed under prohibited or conditional categories can also be imported in designated quantities.
The notification states that, alongside irrevocable letters of credit (LCs) or contracts, imports can now also be conducted through Telegraphic Transfer (TT) systems in specific cases.
Import rules for salt have also been simplified for bond-licensed industrial enterprises. From now on, the customs authority will determine the import quantity based on the approved annual demand and actual utilization. Recommendations from sponsoring organizations will no longer be required in this case.
Another crucial change for the industrial sector is that approved industrial units will be able to import capital machinery for setting up industries without an Import Registration Certificate (IRC). Provisions have also been made to allow the import of necessary spare parts to keep production running smoothly.
Additionally, in the case of private importers, cover notes and insurance policies issued by the Sadharan Bima Corporation, Bangladeshi insurance companies, or foreign insurance companies (where applicable) must be submitted online to the customs authority during goods clearance.
Ministry of Commerce officials stated that these amendments aim to meet the demands of export-oriented industries, boost the production of high-value garments, and streamline the import process.
The new facilities will particularly help expand Bangladesh's share in the global market for man-made fibre-based apparel.

item.title: Baira members: Syndicate conspiracy risks Malaysian labour market yet again
item.description:
Members of a faction of the Bangladesh Association of International Recruiting Agencies (Baira) have expressed concerns that the Malaysian labour market could face renewed risks if the planned conspiracies of dishonest syndicates are not stopped.
They alleged that just as the manpower export process is progressing after a long pause through a joint initiative between Dhaka and Kuala Lumpur, attempts are being made to sabotage the market using misinformation, fake demand letters, and malicious activities.
​Baira members who advocate for quickly sending workers to Malaysia through selected agencies made these allegations at a press conference held at the National Press Club on Monday (September 21).
​Demanding transparency in the worker export process, Atiqur Rahman Biswas, convener of the Labour Market Protection Movement, said: "Initially, 25 licences were approved, but later, through discussions, all eligible licenses were brought under the FWCMS. This is not a syndication; the market is open to all capable and interested license owners."
​Malaysia halted the recruitment of workers from various countries, including Bangladesh, on May 31, 2024.
After a long hiatus, the process of reopening the labour market for Bangladeshi workers began in August of this year.
Thus far, 25 principal and 312 associate recruiting agencies have been approved.
​At the press conference, Baira members claimed that only agencies fulfilling the required conditions have been included in the process this time.
They asserted that no financial transactions were made with any recruiting agency to get listed in the FWCMS. The agencies were selected strictly based on meeting the prescribed qualifications and conditions.
​They noted that workers were sent to Malaysia from Bangladesh through 10 recruiting agencies during 2017-18, and through 101 principal and 250 associate agencies (including BOESL) from August 8, 2022, to May 31, 2024.
Around 476,000 Bangladeshi workers traveled to the country during that timeframe.
​Highlighting how unscrupulous circles are damaging the market, Baira's former senior vice-president Abdul Gafur Bhuiyan said: "Market opponents are spreading confusion by claiming it costs Tk6 lakh to Tk8 lakh. This is ruining the country's image. The host country has its own rules and regulations; we cannot interfere with them."
​The speakers also alleged that certain agencies and middlemen who failed to get listed in the previous process are now trying to obstruct the labour market anew through various programs, press conferences, and the spread of misinformation.
​It was announced at the press conference that Malaysia has approved 25 principal and 312 associate agencies out of a list of 423 agencies submitted by Bangladesh.
The process of sending workers through these agencies is currently progressing.

item.title: Farmers protest fertilizer, fuel price hikes in Jessore
item.description:
The Jessore district unit of Jatiya Krishak Khetmajur Samity (National Peasants and Farm Laborers Association) on Monday submitted a memorandum to the deputy commissioner, protesting alleged fertilizer black marketing, corruption in the agriculture sector and rising diesel and electricity prices.
The organization brought out a procession from its central office in the town at noon. The procession passed through several roads before gathering in front of the Deputy Commissioner’s Office, where the protesters held a rally.
Later, the leaders submitted the memorandum to the deputy commissioner.
In the memorandum, the organization alleged that although fertilizer supplies were adequate during the peak farming season, dealers were not providing farmers with fertilizer according to their requirements.
As a result, farmers were being forced to purchase fertilizer from the open market or black market at prices significantly higher than the government-fixed rates, the organization claimed.
It also alleged irregularities in government-funded demonstration farms under the Department of Agricultural Extension. According to the organization, demonstration farms were supposed to be established during three rice-growing seasons, but the projects were not properly implemented and allocated funds were allegedly misappropriated.
The farmers’ leaders also expressed concern over rising diesel and electricity prices ahead of the upcoming Boro season.
They said frequent load-shedding and high fuel prices were increasing irrigation and production costs, creating additional pressure on farmers.
The organization warned that if the situation continues, farmers may fail to achieve expected yields and could eventually lose their farmland, increasing rural landlessness and posing risks to the country’s food security.
The organization placed four demands, including ensuring fertilizer supplies at fair prices, stopping black-market sales and taking action against unscrupulous traders.
It also demanded an investigation into alleged embezzlement of funds under demonstration farm projects, proper agricultural subsidies for farmers and action against field supervisors allegedly involved in irregularities.
Other demands included direct subsidies on diesel and electricity used for agricultural production, withdrawal of what the organization described as unjustified fuel price hikes, profitable rice prices and government rice procurement centres in every union.
The organization also demanded that the government purchase the full quantity of rice farmers are willing to sell.
Jessore district committee Acting President Mizanur Rahman spoke while the memorandum was being submitted. Central committee Organizing Secretary Taslim-ur-Rahman addressed the rally.
District leaders Monowara Siddiqui Chhobi, Bithika Biswas, Palash Biswas, Sabar Biswas and Sahabuddin Batul, along with local farmers’ leaders, were also present.

item.title: 3 to die in Faruk murder case in Tangail
item.description:
A court in Tangail on Monday sentenced three people to death and four others to life imprisonment in the murder case of former Dainya union parishad chairman and former vice-president of Tangail Sadar Thana BNP Rafiqul Islam Faruk, 13 years after the killing.
Judge Md Faisal Al Mamun of Tangail First Additional District and Sessions Court pronounced the verdict this afternoon, confirmed Public Prosecutor (PP) of the court Md Saidur Rahman Swapan.
The death-row convicts are Saniyat Khan Bappa, former vice-president of Chhatra League and son of former lawmaker Ataur Rahman Khan of Collegepara in Tangail town, Md Azad, son of Afzal Fakir of Kagmara area in Sadar upazila and Shahjahan, son of Shahid Mia of Dainya area. All three are absconding.
The four convicts sentenced to life imprisonment are Md Sujon, son of Latif Mia of Jogani area, Sanowar Hossain, son of Rawshan Ali of Dainya, Shafiqul Islam, son of Md Nurul Islam of Char Kagmara and Ruzbel, son of Nur Box of Chhitki Bari area.
The court also fined each of the death-row convicts Tk 100,000 and each of the life-term convicts Tk 50,000. In default of payment, they will have to serve one year of imprisonment.
Another accused, Sanjit Ghosh, son of Amulya Ghosh of Dainya, was acquitted.
According to the prosecution, Faruk used to live in a rented house in Akurtakur area of Tangail town. On December 20, 2013, he went out for a morning walk around 6.30am.
When he reached Bottola Bazar area, a group of assailants shot and hacked him to death. Police later recovered his body from the scene.
The following day, Faruk's younger brother Lavlu Mia filed a murder case with Tangail Sadar Police Station.
After investigation, the then District Detective Branch Inspector and investigation officer Ashok Kumar Singh submitted a charge sheet against eight people to the court on August 13, 2015.
After completing the reinvestigation, Tangail CID Inspector Rafique Uddin Ahmed submitted another charge sheet on April 29, 2018, against the same eight accused.

item.title: MP Nazrul, first wife accused of torturing second wife, abetting suicide
item.description:
The father of lawmaker Gazi Nazrul Islam’s second wife, Mariam, has accused the MP, his first wife Maksuda Islam and matchmaker Obaidur Rahman of physically and mentally torturing his daughter and abetting her suicide.
Mariam’s father Masum Billah filed the case with Sher-e-Bangla Nagar police naming Nazrul Islam, 75, as the prime accused, Maksuda Islam, 65, as the second accused and Obaidur Rahman, 38, as the third accused.
In the first information report (FIR), Masum said he is a grocery shop owner and has three daughters. Mariam, 19, was his eldest daughter.
He identified Nazrul as Mariam’s husband and Maksuda as his first wife, while describing Obaidur as his brother-in-law.
According to the FIR, Mariam married Nazrul in June under Islamic Shariah. Nazrul, who is a lawmaker, lived with Mariam and his first wife at Flat 203 on the third floor of Building 5 of NAM Bhaban, opposite the National Parliament complex on Manik Mia Avenue under Sher-e-Bangla Nagar police station.
Masum alleged that Obaidur directly instigated the marriage. He said Mariam had repeatedly told her family over the phone that Nazrul and Maksuda subjected her to physical and mental torture after the marriage.
The FIR said Nazrul called Masum at around 5:30pm on Sunday and asked him to come to the residence immediately. Masum then went there by CNG-run auto-rickshaw with his sister-in-law Sufia.
Upon reaching the residence, Masum saw a large number of people and learned that Mariam was hanging from a ceiling fan by a scraf inside a room. He said she was shown through a window and that the room was locked from inside.
In Masum’s presence, witness Md Saidul Islam, 36, broke open the door with the help of Sher-e-Bangla Nagar police, the FIR said. Saidul is a temporary plumber employed by the Public Works Department (PWD), according to the complaint.
Masum said they found Mariam hanging from the ceiling fan with a scarf around her neck. A handwritten suicide note was also found on her bed.
The note reportedly accused someone of betraying Mariam’s trust and referred to a “battle” she had entered believing she would win. “I kept bowing to you again and again because I fell for you. Otherwise, I am not as cheap as you think,” the note reportedly said. It further said: “I entered the battle with him, trusting him completely, but I could not win.”
The note contained further writings, the FIR said.
Masum alleged that after questioning people at the scene, he learned that Mariam might have died by suicide sometime between 3:00pm and 5:30pm.
Later, Sher-e-Bangla Nagar police visited the scene, prepared an inquest report and sent Mariam’s body to the morgue, according to the FIR.

item.title: 17th International Inter-University Short Film Festival begins
item.description:
The 17th International Inter-University Short Film Festival (IIUSFF) began at the TSC premises of Dhaka University on Monday evening, with speakers discussing the festival’s journey and the role of cinema in truth-telling and preserving cultural memory.
Organized by the Dhaka University Film Society (DUFS), the festival began in 2007 in a small room on the 2nd floor of TSC with the slogan “Take Your Camera, Frame Your Dream.”
DUFS President Rehnuma Shahreen said 1,269 films from 92 countries, including Bangladesh, Iran, the United States and Poland, were submitted to this year’s festival.
She said the scale of the festival would have been unimaginable in 2007, when opportunities for communication and networking were limited.
The 3-day main event, running from September 21 to 23, features open screenings of 200 selected short films, discussions with student filmmakers and a live art camp.
The festival is being held with support from UNDP Bangladesh, the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) and the Royal Norwegian Embassy in Dhaka.
Speaking as a guest, film critic and teacher Bidhan Rebeiro referred to the recently released documentary “Naza.”
He said the documentary has sparked debate worldwide by featuring testimonies from former Israeli intelligence officials about the use of artificial intelligence in attacks on Gaza, while its filmmakers have faced threats.
According to Rebeiro, the term “Naza” is used in intelligence circles to describe civilian casualties in such attacks.
He said the Israeli government had threatened to revoke the filmmakers’ citizenship and completely ban the production after the documentary was screened at the Venice and Toronto film festivals.
Rebeiro described the documentary as a “poetry of resistance” and praised its restrained visual language for challenging the global system of aggression.
He also linked this year’s festival theme, “Baul,” to the word “batul,” meaning madness, and said it reflected the social attitudes faced by people in Bangladesh who are interested in studying or pursuing careers in film.
He said cinema should be recognized as a complete and independent discipline rather than merely a vocational subject.
Teacher and film society movement activist Moinuddin Khaled discussed the difference between documentaries and propaganda.
He expressed regret that, despite documentaries being at the roots of cinema, Bangladesh lacks strong documentary records of its folk life and riverine civilization, including group fishing, jute cultivation and boat races.
Referring to Baul music and Lalon songs, he said: “The day we lose Baul songs, we will lose our greatest means of self-expression.”
He described farmers and fishermen as the 2 main pillars sustaining the civilization of the nation.

Two children die of suspected measles in Sylhet, 158 hospitalised
item.description:
Two children died of suspected measles while 158 patients were admitted to hospitals in Sylhet division in the past 24 hours.
No confirmed measles cases were recorded during the period, according to the latest data from the Divisional Health Department.
The deaths have raised the division’s combined toll from confirmed and suspected measles to 172 since January 1. Of them, 10 were confirmed measles deaths and 162 were suspected cases. A total of 1,053 confirmed measles cases have been recorded this year.
The latest fatalities were seven-month-old Samya of Shalla upazila in Sunamganj and two-year-two-month-old Faria of Tahirpur in the district. Both died while undergoing treatment at Sylhet MAG Osmani Medical College Hospital.
Of the 158 newly admitted patients, 53 were admitted to Shaheed Shamsuddin Ahmed Hospital and 45 to Osmani Medical College Hospital. Sunamganj Sadar Hospital admitted 43, while Moulvibazar Sadar Hospital received 11.
Currently, 535 suspected patients are receiving treatment across the division, including 189 at Osmani Medical College Hospital and 167 at Shaheed Shamsuddin Ahmed Hospital.
Sylhet has recorded the highest number of confirmed cases at 385, followed by Sunamganj with 357, Moulvibazar 158 and Habiganj 153.
The health department said necessary treatment and healthcare services are being provided at hospitals and local health facilities.

item.title: Fuel price hike disrupts public transport in Chittagong
item.description:
Public transport services in Chittagong have declined following the government’s fuel price hike, leaving commuters facing longer waits, overcrowded vehicles and allegations of higher fares.
Since on Monday morning, large crowds of passengers have gathered at major intersections and bus stops as fewer buses and human haulers operated on some routes. When vehicles arrived, passengers rushed to board, with many unable to get on as buses and human haulers were already packed.
At around 9am, passengers at Muradpur said they had been waiting for extended periods to reach their destinations. “I have been waiting for about 30 minutes to go to Agrabad. The number of public transport vehicles has dropped, and the ones arriving are overcrowded,” passenger Nurul Islam said.
Another passenger, Md Musa, alleged that some operators were charging higher fares, citing the fuel price increase.
The Muradpur-Kotwali route appeared particularly affected, with few public transport options available. Passengers alleged that many maxis were carrying passengers only as far as Chawkbazar, forcing commuters to change vehicles to reach Kotwali. This has increased both travel time and transport costs.
Shahidul Islam, joint secretary of the Chittagong Metropolitan Transport Owners’ Association, said the fuel price hike would inevitably affect public transport operations. “However, there is no justification for charging passengers extra fares now. No instruction has been issued to increase fares. If such an instruction comes, fares will be revised accordingly,” he said.
He said some vehicle owners may have kept their vehicles off the roads due to higher operating costs, despite instructions to keep all vehicles running.
According to the association, 1,300 buses operate on 18 routes in the city, while 1,800-1,900 human haulers operate on 22 routes.
The government announced a Tk20-per-litre increase in diesel, octane and petrol prices on Sunday night. The new prices took effect at midnight. Diesel, widely used by buses and other public transport vehicles, rose from Tk115 to Tk135 per litre.

Pubali Bank, BB sign agreements under two refinance schemes
item.description:
To expand financing for sustainable industrialization, environment-friendly production and the development of a technology-driven economy, Pubali Bank PLC. has joined Bangladesh Bank’s ‘Refinance Scheme for Green Factory Building and Green Industry Sector’ and ‘Refinance Scheme for Development of the Information and Communication Technology Sector’.
Each scheme has a fund size of Tk1,000 crore.
Pubali Bank has signed separate Participation Agreements with Bangladesh Bank for the two schemes administered by the Sustainable Finance Department of Bangladesh Bank.
At the agreement signing ceremony held at the Bangladesh Bank Head Office on the same day, Director of the Sustainable Finance Department of Bangladesh Bank AKM Nurunnabi and managing director of Pubali Bank PLC Mohammad Ali signed the agreements on behalf of their respective institutions.
Also present were deputy managing director of Pubali Bank PLC Mohammad Esha and general manager & head of RMG Division Md Nazrul Islam Sarker, along with other senior officials of Bangladesh Bank and Pubali Bank.
To support the implementation of various long-term plans announced by the Government of Bangladesh—including the Perspective Plan of Bangladesh, National Sustainable Development Strategy, Intended Nationally Determined Contributions (INDCs), Bangladesh Delta Plan 2100 and Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)—and to make the country’s financial sector more environment-friendly, Bangladesh Bank has established the Tk1,000 crore ‘Refinance Scheme for Green Factory Building and Green Industry Sector’ to encourage financing for green factory buildings and green industries.
The scheme will expand financing opportunities for the establishment of green factory buildings, green industries and other environmentally responsible industrial initiatives.
It is expected to promote green investment while further accelerating the adoption of sustainable production practices and responsible industrialization.
Meanwhile, under the ‘Refinance Scheme for Development of the Information and Communication Technology Sector’, Bangladesh Bank has established a Tk1,000 crore fund.
The scheme aims to enhance the efficiency and competitiveness of the ICT sector through the adoption of modern and sustainable technologies, develop human resources, expand technology-driven enterprises, and support the development of new technologies and services aligned with the Fourth Industrial Revolution.
The facility covers various technology-driven initiatives, including software development, artificial intelligence, cyber security, fintech, cloud computing, e-commerce, robotics and semiconductors.
Through participation in these two refinance schemes, Pubali Bank PLC. will further strengthen its role in expanding financing for environment-friendly industrial initiatives and the promising information and communication technology sector.
The initiatives are expected to widen access to financing for eligible entrepreneurs and institutions while contributing to sustainable industrialization, technological capacity building, innovation and employment generation in the country.

item.title: Ambassador: Brands like Walton should be promoted more in global market
item.description:
Bangladesh Ambassador to Nepal Md Shafiqur Rahman has called for concerted efforts to further strengthen the presence of Bangladeshi brands like Walton in the global market.
He said Walton has been doing remarkable work in Bangladesh’s hi-tech industry. By manufacturing international-standard technology products, the company reduced the country’s import dependency and saved a significant amount of foreign currency. At the same time, Walton is contributing to foreign currency earnings by exporting its products to different countries across the world.
The Ambassador made the remarks as the chief guest at a special program of Walton Plaza, Bangladesh’s leading sales and service provider of electronics and technology products, titled ‘Tushar Jatra’, held on Saturday (September 19) at The Soaltee in Kathmandu, Nepal.
Among others, SM Mahbubul Alam, managing director of Walton Hi-Tech Industries PLC and managing partner of Walton Plaza; Pranil Thapa, chairman of Nepal’s renowned Thapa Business Group; Pranimesh Thapa, director of Thapa Business Group; and senior officials of Walton attended the program.
Ambassador Md Shafiqur Rahman said: “Walton is doing remarkable work in Bangladesh’s hi-tech sector. The quality of Walton’s locally manufactured hi-tech products is top-notch. With these products, Walton is competing with other international brands in the global market and establishing a strong position. This is a matter of great pride for the people of Bangladesh.”
He further said that the local production of high-quality hi-tech products is reducing Bangladesh’s dependence on imports and saving a substantial amount of foreign currency. At the same time, Walton is earning foreign currency by exporting technology products to different countries around the world.
“Bangladeshi brands like Walton should be promoted more extensively in the international market. Bangladeshi ambassadors serving in different countries will also play a role in expanding the global market for local brands through economic diplomacy,” he added.
SM Mahbubul Alam, managing director of Walton Hi-Tech Industries PLC and managing partner of Walton Plaza, said Nepal is a highly important market for Walton. The company is working to make international-standard technology products available to Nepali consumers at affordable prices, just as it does in Bangladesh. Walton aims to further expand its operations in Nepal by building long-term relationships and mutual trust with local business partners.
Pranimesh Thapa, director of Thapa Business Group, said: “We are proud to have been part of Walton’s journey in Nepal for more than eight years. Thapa Business Group is committed to further expanding Walton’s presence across Nepal through innovative and quality products. We will continue working with our business partners to provide better services to customers and establish Walton as one of Nepal’s leading technology product brands.”
Md Rayhan, managing director of Walton Plaza, provided important guidelines to Walton Plaza officials, particularly on modern marketing and sales management.
Mofizur Rahman Jakir, deputy managing director of Walton Hi-Tech Industries PLC, and MM Nazmul Hasan, head of sales at Walton Plaza, also spoke at the program.
The event was conducted by Amin Khan, senior executive director of Walton Hi-Tech Industries PLC and noted film actor. It also featured a Nepal tour video presentation, raffle draw and cultural performances.

item.title: ONE Bank, BYD Bangladesh to facilitate new EV financing
item.description:
ONE Bank PLC has signed an MoU with BYD Bangladesh to facilitate convenient and attractive financing solutions for customers purchasing New Energy Vehicles (NEVs).
Under this collaboration, ONE Bank PLC will offer competitive interest rates and expedited loan processing facilities to customers purchasing BYD vehicles.
The initiative aims to make NEV financing more accessible and convenient for customers while supporting the adoption of environmentally friendly mobility solutions in Bangladesh.
On behalf of the two organizations, the MoU was signed by Amid Sakif Khan, managing director, BYD Bangladesh, and Mohammad Shahid Ul Haque, executive vice president & head of retail banking division of ONE Bank PLC.
The ceremony was also attended by Ferdowsur Rahman, chief financial officer; BYD Bangladesh; Methun Bhattacharjee, head of business development BYD Bangladesh; Kazi Ziaul Islam, deputy managing director and head of financial services and public sector; ONE Bank PLC; Iftekhar Ahmed Zafar, deputy managing director and head of transaction and investment banking, ONE Bank PLC, and senior officials from both the organizations.
BYD, a global leader in New Energy Vehicles (NEVs), entered the Bangladesh automobile market in 2024 through its official distributor.
The brand offers a growing range of advanced electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles, supported by modern showrooms and comprehensive after-sales service facilities.
With a strong focus on innovative technology, sustainable mobility, and energy-efficient transportation, BYD is contributing to the development of Bangladesh’s emerging electric vehicle market.
The collaboration between ONE Bank PLC and BYD Bangladesh reflects a shared commitment to promoting sustainable transportation and providing customers with accessible financing solutions for next-generation vehicles.

item.title: Nagad, IFIC Bank to introduce interoperable cardless cash withdrawal facility
item.description:
Nagad, one of Bangladesh’s leading mobile financial services (MFS) providers, has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with IFIC Bank PLC to launch an interoperable cardless cash withdrawal facility.
Under this agreement, Nagad customers will be able to withdraw cash from all IFIC Bank Automated Teller Machines (ATMs) across the country without using a physical card.
The agreement was signed at IFIC Bank’s head office in Dhaka.
High-ranking officials from both organizations were present at the signing ceremony, highlighting the strategic importance of this collaboration in enhancing financial inclusion and expanding digital banking services in Bangladesh.
Through this partnership, Nagad users can generate a secure, temporary transaction code or QR-based request via the Nagad mobile app to withdraw cash directly from IFIC Bank ATMs nationwide.
This initiative aims to provide customers with greater convenience, seamless interoperability between bank channels and mobile wallets, and enhanced security for cash transactions.
Speaking at the event, representatives from both Nagad and IFIC Bank emphasized their shared commitment to driving digital innovation, reducing dependence on physical cards, and building a more robust cashless ecosystem across the country.

item.title: Nationwide digital dengue awareness campaign launched
item.description:
A three-month nationwide digital awareness campaign has been launched to combat dengue, with State Minister for Health Dr MA Muhit urging citizens, particularly young people and social media content creators, to participate actively.
In a statement issued Monday, Muhit said dengue cannot be fully controlled through administrative measures or insecticide spraying alone, stressing the importance of individual and collective awareness.
He said social media can play a significant role in spreading timely information and reducing dengue risks, urging content creators and influencers to produce and share awareness materials, including videos, reels, stories, infographics and posts.
“Content creators can effectively communicate important messages on dengue prevention, including eliminating stagnant water and seeking medical attention promptly after symptoms appear,” the state minister said.
Many content creators have already joined the campaign facilitated by the Ministry of Health.
Over the next three months, social media platforms will be used to disseminate information on destroying Aedes mosquito breeding sites, recognizing dengue symptoms and providing initial care.
The state minister urged people to keep their homes and workplaces clean and help spread dengue prevention messages online as part of the national campaign.

item.title: Ashulia factory fire: Death toll rises to 8
item.description:
The death toll from a fire at a readymade garment factory in Jamgara of Ashulia has risen to eight after another victim died of his injuries on Sunday night.
The victim, a vegetable vendor whose identity could not immediately be known, succumbed to his injuries while undergoing treatment at Dhaka Medical College and Hospital, said Shahabuddin, senior station officer of Zirabo Fire Service.
The fire broke out at the F&F factory of Preeti Group in the Jamgara Chowrasta area at around 6:45pm on Sunday.
According to the Fire Service, the fire was triggered when a gas cylinder exploded while being unloaded from a covered van.
Four firefighting units rushed to the scene and brought the blaze under control around 3:30am.
Shahabuddin said firefighters struggled to reach the factory because of severe traffic congestion and poor road conditions, where construction work for the Ashulia Elevated Expressway is underway.
Litton Mia, a line man at a nearby garment factory and a witness, said the fire spread through the factory following a loud explosion of a gas cylinder.
The authorities are investigating the circumstances surrounding the fire.

item.title: Man kills mother, sister-in-law, 8-month-old niece in Comilla
item.description:
A man has allegedly hacked his mother and sister-in-law to death and killed his eight-month-old niece by slamming her against the ground in Debidwar, Comilla.
The incident occurred around 8:30am on Monday, at the house of late Mostafa Master in the southern part of Barshalghar village in the upazila.
Following the incident, local residents caught the accused, Imon, 24, red-handed and locked him inside a room. He is the son of the late Farid Mia of the same house.
According to locals, Imon’s mother, Peyaara Begum, and his eight-month-old niece died at the scene. His sister-in-law, Rabeya Begum, who sustained critical injuries in the attack, died on the way to hospital.
Local sources said Imon suddenly became agitated around 8:30am and hacked his mother to death with a machete. He then slammed his eight-month-old niece against the ground, killing her. When Rabeya Begum came forward to stop him, he attacked her indiscriminately with the machete, leaving her critically injured.
Locals later rescued Rabeya and rushed her to hospital for treatment, while detaining Imon in a nearby room.
Debidwar police station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Md Moniruzzaman confirmed the incident, saying police were on their way to the scene after receiving the report.
“Preliminarily, we have learned that Imon had been ill for a long time. However, it is not yet clear what prompted the brutal killings. The matter will become clear after we reach the scene and conduct a detailed investigation,” he said.

item.title: Bus set ablaze while parked in Narayanganj
item.description:
A Nilachal Paribahan bus was set ablaze while parked by the roadside in Siddhirganj, Narayanganj, early Monday.
The incident occurred around 2am on a new road beside the SO Eidgah ground in Ward 6 of Narayanganj City Corporation. No casualties were reported.
According to locals, the bus, which operates on the Chittagong Road-Paturia route, was parked by the roadside when miscreants allegedly set it on fire between 1:35am and 2am.
Two units from Adamjee Fire Station responded to the incident and brought the blaze under control. The bus was severely damaged, with its seats and other parts gutted by the fire.
Abdullah Al Arefin, deputy director of Narayanganj Fire Service, said the bus was extensively damaged, but no one was injured.
The cause of the fire has not yet been determined.
Confirming the incident, Tarek Al Mehedi, additional superintendent of police (Crime) of Narayanganj district, said: “We are reviewing CCTV footage to identify those involved in the incident. Legal action regarding the matter is currently underway.”

item.title: Chief Whip Moni leaves Dhaka for Malaysia

item.title: Gazi Nazrul, first wife arrested over second wife’s death
item.description:
A case has been filed on charges of abetting suicide following the recovery of the hanging body of Mariyam Khatun, second wife of Satkhira-4 MP Gazi Nazrul Islam, from a flat at the NAM Bhaban in the capital.
Mariyam’s father, Masum Billah, filed the case at Sher-e-Bangla Nagar Police Station late Sunday night. Gazi Nazrul, his first wife Maksuda Begum and Mariam’s maternal uncle Obaidur Rahman have been named as the three accused.
Dhaka Metropolitan Police Tejgaon Division Deputy Commissioner Md Ibne Mizan told the media that Gazi Nazrul and his first wife have been shown arrested, but Obaidur Rahman remains at large.
The 19-year-old woman, whom Satkhira-4 MP Gazi Nazrul Islam identified as his second wife amid a sensational controversy two months ago, was found hanging at his NAM Bhaban flat in Dhaka on Sunday, prompting police to take the lawmaker and his first wife to the police station for questioning.
Mariyam Khatun’s death brings Nazrul and the disputed circumstances surrounding their marriage back under scrutiny barely two months after the controversy led to his expulsion from Jamaat-e-Islami.
The controversy erupted on July 20 when video clips showing Nazrul in an intimate setting with a young woman began circulating widely on social media.
Nazrul subsequently identified the woman as Mariyam and rejected allegations that he was involved in an extramarital relationship. He said she was his legally married second wife.
According to Nazrul, he had married Mariyam on June 17 at her father’s residence in Shyamnagar, Satkhira, with the consent of both families and his first wife, Maksuda Islam.
Nazrul said that on July 13 he went with both wives to an office belonging to Mariyam’s father, Md Masum Billah, in Moghbazar.
He alleged that while they were there, Mariyam’s maternal uncle Obaidullah and several others entered the room, held them hostage and extorted Tk1 lakh.
He further alleged that demands for additional money followed and that private footage was later circulated because of a family dispute.
Maksuda subsequently appeared in a video message confirming that Nazrul had married Mariyam and protesting what she described as slander surrounding their relationship.
Mariyam herself also appeared publicly, wearing a face mask, and identified Nazrul as her husband.
She said the marriage was neither secret nor illicit and maintained that it had taken place with the consent of both families.
But questions subsequently emerged over the chronology of the marriage.
A CV attributed to Mariyam circulated online bearing Nazrul’s signature and a recommendation dated June 22, five days after the date on which Nazrul said they had married.
The CV reportedly listed her marital status as “unmarried”.
Further questions arose over the marriage registration.
The marriage registrar whose name appeared on the certificate later said he had not been present at the purported wedding and did not know when or where the marriage had taken place.
Reporting at the time said Nazrul maintained that the marriage occurred on June 17.
The controversy intensified as multiple video clips circulated.
In one, Nazrul and Mariyam were confronted by several men in a room.
Nazrul’s subsequent account was that the incident involved extortion and that the intimate footage had been distributed without consent.
The controversy quickly became a political crisis for Jamaat.
After initially saying it would investigate the allegations, the party’s Central Executive Council met on July 22 and expelled Nazrul under Article 62 of its constitution, saying an organisational investigation had found evidence of “moral misconduct”.
Jamaat subsequently formally informed both the Speaker and the Election Commission of the decision.
Nazrul had been elected from Satkhira-4 on Jamaat’s scales symbol in the February election.
His expulsion was described at the time as the first instance of Jamaat expelling one of its sitting lawmakers.
Two months after that controversy, the young woman at its centre has now been found dead inside the MPs’ residential complex.
CID forensic investigators reached the scene on Sunday evening as police began examining the circumstances surrounding Mariyam’s death.
With police yet to determine whether she took her own life or was killed, the cause and circumstances of her death remain under investigation.

item.title: Chevron Bangladesh launches Community Tree Guardianship initiative
item.description:
Chevron Bangladesh has launched a community-based Tree Guardianship initiative in partnership with Green Savers which is designed to expand green cover and support families living near its operational areas in Habiganj and Moulavibazar.
As part of the initiative, each Tree Guardian household will receive ten fruit bearing tree saplings, following a crop calendar, that includes mango, black plum (jamun), jackfruit, lychee, guava, lemon, hog plum (amra), custard apple, Indian gooseberry (amla) and jujube (boroi).
In total, 3,190 fruit tree saplings will be distributed, helping expand green cover while creating long-term environmental and socioeconomic benefits for participating families.
The participating households were selected following a field assessment that considered available space and the potential for long-term care of the trees.
Each participating family will serve as a "Tree Guardian” taking responsibility for household-level planting, protection and maintenance of the saplings.
The recently held event was graced by Md Abul Kalam Azad, director, Department of Environment (DoE), Sylhet Divisional Office as chief guest; Kaelie Knight Holder, general manager operations, Chevron Bangladesh; Muhammad Imrul Kabir, director, corporate affairs, Chevron Bangladesh; AKM Arif Akter, head of community engagement & sustainability, Chevron Bangladesh; Ahsan Rony, CEO of Green Savers, including other representatives from Department of Environment, Sylhet Forest Division, Mirzapur Union Parishad and representatives from Green Savers; employees of Chevron Bangladesh; and the dedicated Tree Guardians, whose efforts continue to support the long-term sustainability of the plantation initiative.
“Initiatives like this play an important role in advancing environmental sustainability and supporting the government’s goal of planting 250 million trees within five years. Through collective action and long-term commitment, we can build a greener, cleaner, and more sustainable Bangladesh,” said Md Abul Kalam Azad, director, Department of Environment (DoE), Sylhet Divisional Office.
Muhammad Imrul Kabir, director corporate affairs, Chevron Bangladesh, said: “This initiative reflects our commitment to working with neighboring communities to promote environmental stewardship and create meaningful benefits for participating families. By placing local residents at the center of the program, we hope to encourage long-term care of the trees and strengthen shared responsibility for the surrounding environment.”
“At Chevron Bangladesh, we believe safe and reliable operations are built on strong partnerships with the communities where we operate. Through the Tree Guardianship Program, we are working together to promote environmental stewardship, strengthen community partnerships, and create lasting value for future generations,” said Kaelie Knight Holder, general manager operations, Chevron Bangladesh.
As part of the initiative, Tree Guardians will receive practical training on soil preparation, plantation techniques, tree care, and long-term maintenance.
The community stewardship approach is intended to support tree survival while contributing to food security, household nutrition and potential supplementary income opportunities for participating families.
The Tree Guardianship initiative is designed to encourage community participation in environmental conservation and establish a greener landscape around pipeline-adjacent communities.
It also aims to strengthen local awareness and a sense of shared responsibility toward the safety and security of nearby pipeline infrastructure.

item.title: Opratim’s mother’s iPhone recovered from Tuhin’s home
item.description:
Police have recovered the iPhone belonging to 13-year-old Ishiyat Shahriar Opratim’s mother from the home of Tuhin, who was detained in connection with the boy’s death in Comilla.
Mofiz Uddin Bhuiyan, in-charge of the Kotbari Police Outpost, confirmed the matter on Saturday night.
He said police recovered the iPhone during a raid at Tuhin’s house in the Sananda area of Lalmai Hill, near Comilla University.
Opratim, a seventh-grade student at Comilla Border Guard Public School, had been missing since Friday afternoon. His body was found in Sananda area around 1:00pm on Saturday.
His mother, Dr Nahida Begum, is an associate professor in the Department of Bangla at Comilla University. She lived in a rented house in the Kotbari-Gandhamati area.
Police have detained three people Tuhin, Anas and Fahim in connection with the death. All three are aged between 18 and 20.
Inspector Mofiz Uddin said the other two were detained in the evening based on information obtained from Tuhin during questioning. Tuhin was detained around 3:00pm on Saturday.

item.description:
