The detainee was identified as Aminul Islam Shawon.
Police said Shawon was attempting to set fire to the bus around 2:15am when bus staff and local people noticed the incident and rushed to the spot.
Patrol police also arrived at the scene and detained him.
An agitated crowd beat up Shawon during the detention, leaving him injured, said Niaz Mehedi, additional deputy commissioner (Media) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police on Sunday afternoon.
He was later taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital for treatment.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,057 as four die in 24 hours
item.description:
Four more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Sunday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 1,057.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all four of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 956, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 101, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
Among the four new suspected fatalities, the highest concentration was recorded in Dhaka, with two deaths reported in both the Dhaka division and Dhaka district.
A total of 1,148 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Sunday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 179,814.
During the same period, 88 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 20,562.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 158,589 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 152,225 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.title: Jatrabari crude bomb blasts: Four sent to jail, remand hearing Tuesday
item.description:
Four people, including a leader of the banned Awami League, have been sent to jail in a case filed over multiple crude bomb explosions in front of Jatrabari Police Station in Dhaka. The court has scheduled a hearing for Tuesday on a five-day remand plea against them.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Md Monirul Islam passed the order on Sunday.
The accused are Md Rayhan Uddin, 35, office secretary of the Awami League’s Unit 6 under Ward 32 of Bangshal Police Station area of Dhaka South City, Russell Khan, 32, Ala Uddin, 28, and Abdullah Mashhur Ashrafi, 20.
DB police Inspector Mohammad Golam Mostofa, investigation officer of the Wari zone, sought five days’ remand for the accused.
SI Mohin Uddin of the prosecution department confirmed the matter, saying, “The investigation officer did not appear before the court. Therefore, the accused were sent to jail and the remand hearing was scheduled for Tuesday.”
Several crude bombs exploded in front of Jatrabari Police Station on the night of September 18.
After identifying a suspect from CCTV footage, police arrested Rayhan Uddin during a raid in the Bangshal area on Saturday.
Based on information provided by Rayhan, police later recovered four unexploded crude bombs wrapped in red cellophane tape and concealed in a sack of brick chips beside a pillar in the ground-floor parking area of a 10-storey building on Zain Saha Road in Lalbagh around 12:15am. The DMP bomb disposal unit later defused the devices.
Acting on information obtained during Rayhan’s interrogation, police conducted a raid in the Dogair area of Demra and arrested Russell, Ala Uddin and Abdullah.
Meanwhile, Jatrabari Police Station SI Jewel Rana filed a case under the Explosives Act on Saturday over the crude bomb explosions.

item.title: Stakeholders call for stronger media self-regulation, accountability
item.description:
Media stakeholders have called for stronger self-regulation mechanisms to strengthen public trust in the media by ensuring editorial independence and accountability of owners, protecting journalists’ safety, and upholding professional standards.
They also agreed that enforcing editorial policies, ensuring transparency and accountability in management, and providing accessible grievance mechanisms can strengthen accountability in the news media.
They said these measures would help restore public trust by upholding ethical standards while balancing editorial independence with accountability.
The observations came at a divisional consultation held in Khulna by the Media Resources Development Initiative (MRDI) to discuss improving journalism’s professional and ethical standards and developing an effective framework for media self-regulation in Bangladesh.
MRDI launched the consultation series with the Khulna session under the Canada Fund for Local Initiatives, funded by the Canadian High Commission in Bangladesh.
News media owners and publishers, editors, news managers and gatekeepers, leaders of journalist unions and associations, university teachers and civil society representatives took part in the discussion.
MRDI Executive Director Hasibur Rahman called for continued advocacy on media self-regulation under the organization’s 2025–2030 strategic action plan, saying effective self-regulation would limit external interference.
He said press freedom depends on public trust, urging news outlets to establish accountability mechanisms and develop separate codes of conduct for journalists, editors and owners.
Speaking at the event, former Media Reform Commission chief and The Daily Star consulting editor Kamal Ahmed urged the government to quickly outline its plan for an independent Media Commission, saying it should promote self-regulation and allow the media to correct its own mistakes.
He criticised plans to increase penalties under the Cyber Security Act without clearly defining offences, warning that tougher laws alone would not resolve the media’s current challenges and could encourage self-censorship instead of self-regulation.
Participants agreed that sustainable self-regulation requires strong and independent editorial policies capable of resisting pressure from the government, media owners, advertisers and political actors.
Shamima Sultana Shilu, executive director of Manob Seba O Samajik Unnayan Sangstha, said journalists must perform their duties in a way that leaves no room for external interference while abiding by the law.
She stressed the importance of proper training before entering the journalism profession, saying it is essential for maintaining professional and ethical standards in journalism and ensuring responsible reporting.
On journalists’ working conditions, participants agreed that ethical journalism cannot be separated from financial security. They called on media owners to ensure timely payment of salaries, formal appointment letters, lawful benefits and a safe working environment.
Hedait Hossain Molla, joint secretary general of the Bangladesh Federal Union of Journalists, said a lack of transparency and integrity in media outlets’ financial practices undermines professionals’ rights and accountability.
He called for clear policies to protect the rights of news media professionals, noting that there is no specific legal framework governing appointment letters and that media organizations follow varying practices. He urged the development of a universal, legally compliant framework for appointment letters.
Sara Monami Hossain, head of the Department of Mass Communication and Journalism at Khulna University, said mainstream media, particularly national news organisations, have systems for information verification and fact-checking.
She said reliable and relevant information is more important in journalism than the volume of information, adding that journalists must assess whether information or an event is genuinely newsworthy before publishing or reporting it.

item.title: Case filed over death of North Western University student
item.description:
A case has been filed over the death of North Western University student Md Azmul Hossain at a mess near Khulna University, accusing four Khulna University students and 20–25 unidentified people.
Harintana police station Officer-in-Charge Md Iqbal Hossain said Saturday night that Azmul’s father, Qutub Uddin, filed the case at the police station.
The case was filed under Sections 302 and 34 of the Penal Code, with 4 people named as accused and another 20–25 unidentified people accused.
All 4 named accused are students of Khulna University.
Md Iqbal Hossain said: “We have learnt that there was already a dispute between them. They were dissatisfied over the use of other people’s clothes and other matters.”
He said no one had been arrested in the case as of Saturday night.
According to the first information report, Azmul was beaten at a mess in Masjid Goli on Islamnagar Road, opposite Khulna University’s Khan Jahan Ali Hall, also known as Khaja Hall, after he was accused of theft.
At one point, he fell from the roof of the 4-storey building.
He was taken to Khulna Medical College Hospital in critical condition and died while undergoing treatment.
According to police and local sources, Azmul ate food at the mess without giving a meal on Friday night. Angered by this and later accusing him of theft, several students of the mess and some local people beat him.
At one point, he was taken to the roof of the building, where he was allegedly subjected to abuse. His hair was also cut, and evidence of this was found at the scene.
He later fell from the building and suffered serious injuries. Around 1:30am, several youths took Azmul to Khulna Medical College Hospital in critical condition.
Hospital sources said there were marks of injuries on different parts of his body. He died after being admitted while undergoing treatment.
Doctors initially suspected excessive blood loss but said the exact cause of death would be confirmed after the post-mortem report.
Azmul Hossain was a 1st-year student of the English Department at North Western University. His home was in Bara Sholua village under Darshana police station in Chuadanga.
He lived in a rented mess in Masjid Goli in the area adjacent to Khulna University.
Meanwhile, Azmul’s family alleged that a phone call was made to them during the incident demanding Tk 100,000. The phone was later found switched off.
Police said they were verifying the allegation.

item.title: ILO: Bangladeshi women earn up to 25% less than men
item.description:
Women in Bangladesh continue to face steep earnings disparities, taking home 22% to 25% less per month than their male counterparts—translating to roughly Tk750 to Tk780 for every Tk1,000 earned by men, according to a report by the International Labour Organization (ILO) titled "The Gender Pay Gap in Bangladesh: Trends, Causes and Policy Options" .
While this disparity is slightly lower than in regional neighbors such as Pakistan, Afghanistan, India, and Sri Lanka, it still exceeds the global average.
Crucially, statistical decomposition reveals that the vast majority of this disparity cannot be explained by observable factors like education, sector of employment, or job role, pointing directly toward pervasive direct and indirect workplace discrimination.
Beyond raw wage numbers, female participation in the formal labour force remains constrained.
Women represent only 17% of all wage employees nationwide, and while female employment has reached 40.2%, only 19% of working women hold salaried wage roles, compared to 48% of working men.
Furthermore, female workers hold a mere 6.2% of managerial positions across the country, marking one of the lowest shares in South Asia.
This earning gap also widens dramatically with age, expanding from 16% for youth (ages 15–24) up to 43% for older workers (ages 55–64), reflecting the long-term career interruptions and structural penalties associated with childbirth and family care.
Although higher education helps narrow the gap from nearly 40% among those with less than basic education to 20% for advanced degree holders, it fails to eliminate it entirely.
Informality further exacerbates the issue, with informal workers facing a pay gap of 33% compared to 17% in formal settings, where legal standards offer greater baseline protection.
Out of 22 sectors analyzed, 20 show a positive gender pay gap, including female-dominated industries like garment manufacturing, where 41% of female wage earners work and face a monthly pay gap of 49%.
Two main structural drivers underpin this persistent disparity: the undervaluation of female-dominated sectors and an unequal distribution of unpaid domestic work.
Sectors with heavy female concentration, such as education and domestic work, consistently offer lower average wages across the board.
Simultaneously, employed women spend an average of 27.7 hours per week on household chores compared to just 7.6 hours spent by men.
Combining paid employment and household responsibilities, women work a total of 73.7 hours per week versus 59 hours for men.
Notably, among the subgroup of workers who perform no household chores at all, the pay gap turns negative, meaning women in that specific category actually earn more than men.
Although constitutional protections and equal pay clauses exist under the Bangladesh Labour Act, implementation gaps persist due to narrow interpretations, incomplete minimum wage board coverage, and direct employer liability for maternity benefits, which can disincentivize female hiring.
To systematically close this gap, the ILO and national stakeholders recommend establishing objective job evaluation systems to enforce equal pay for work of equal value, expanding Minimum Wage Board coverage to unrepresented female-heavy sectors, shifting maternity leave financing away from direct employer liabilities, increasing access to public childcare and flexible work arrangements, and strengthening the labour inspectorate to detect and penalize gender-based pay discrimination.

item.title: President urges Coast Guard to step up efforts to protect coastal security, resources
item.description:
President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on Sunday urged the Bangladesh Coast Guard to take more effective measures to maintain law and order and strengthen security in coastal areas, as well as combat drug smuggling and human trafficking.
He made the remarks when the Director General of the Bangladesh Coast Guard, Rear Admiral Md Moinul Hassan, paid a courtesy call on him at Bangabhaban.
President's Press Secretary Md Sarwar Alam briefed reporters after the meeting.
The president also called upon the Coast Guard to strengthen efforts to conserve fisheries and natural resources, protect the environment and prevent water pollution.
He said the government is committed to developing the Coast Guard into a modern and efficient force capable of protecting the country's vast coastal areas and maritime boundary.
“To this end, the government is working to modernise the force and ensure appropriate training for its members,” Mirza Fakhrul said.
He also urged the Coast Guard to remain vigilant against illegal fishing in the country's maritime territory.
During the meeting, the Coast Guard director general briefed the president on the force's overall activities and progress in procuring new patrol boats and modern rescue helicopters and establishing an aviation wing to enhance its operational capabilities.
He sought the president's cooperation in discharging his responsibilities.
Mirza Fakhrul assured him of all-out cooperation for the development of the force.
The president's secretaries and senior officials concerned were present during the meeting.

item.title: PM Tarique to deliver UNGA speech in Bangla
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman will deliver his address in Bangla at the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA), Foreign Secretary Asad Alam Siam has said.
He made the statement while responding to questions from journalists at a briefing at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Sunday.
In his address, the prime minister is expected to highlight Bangladesh’s democratic progress, the rule of law and accountability, global peace and security, climate change, sustainable development and economic cooperation.
He will also speak on youth and women’s empowerment, education and health, the Rohingya crisis, equitable and inclusive access to modern technology, and reform of the multilateral system.

item.title: Early morning rain causes waterlogging, commuter woes in Dhaka
item.description:
Heavy rain since early Sunday has submerged roads and lanes across Dhaka, causing waterlogging and disrupting commuters on the first working day of the week.
Torrential rain accompanied by gusty winds began around 4am. Although the winds later subsided, rain continued intermittently with lightning.
Waterlogging was reported in several low-lying areas, including Mirpur, Uttara, Badda, Dhanmondi, Mugda, Khilgaon, Sabujbagh, Goran, Maniknagar, Taltala, Motijheel, Malibagh, Arambagh, Gulistan and Paltan.
Water levels reached knee to waist height in some areas, disrupting traffic and causing difficulties for office-goers, students, businesses and residents.
Roads in Sipahibagh, Mugda and Goran were submerged. Several shops in the Maniknagar commercial area were flooded, causing losses for business owners.
Traffic movement was also disrupted from Arambagh intersection towards Fakirapul and Kakrail, where water reached knee to waist height. In Malibagh, water overflowed from roads and footpaths and entered several shops.
The waterlogging also affected rickshaw and public transport services. Many passengers had to wait for extended periods, while some said they were charged higher-than-usual fares to reach their destinations.
Sarwar Hossain, who was travelling from Khilgaon to his office in Motijheel, said ongoing roadwork had made movement difficult even before the rain.
“The early morning rain made the condition of the roads even worse. Anyone travelling through the area for work had to face considerable hardship,” he said.
Local residents said waterlogging recurs every monsoon because of inadequate drainage, debris-filled drains and pipelines, and a lack of regular maintenance.
Abdus Salam, a government employee at the Ministry of Finance, said he encountered waterlogged roads after leaving his home in Rampura and had to wait for a bus.
He said the road from Rampura to Abul Hotel was relatively clear, but significant water had accumulated between Mouchak and Kakrail, making his journey to the office difficult.
Alamin, a Rampura resident, told Bangla Tribune that continuous rain had caused water to accumulate on the streets and enter several roadside shops.
Rafiqul Islam, deputy commissioner of the Tejgaon Traffic Division, said water had accumulated on roads in some parts of the division.
“While this is causing some difficulties for vehicular movement, there are no major traffic jams. Our traffic personnel are performing their regular duties, and so far, there have been no major problems,” he said.
Meanwhile, Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) said heavy rain accompanied by thunderstorms, which began at around 4am, had caused temporary waterlogging in some low-lying areas and sloping roads under its jurisdiction.
The DSCC said cleaning staff from its Waste Management Department and emergency response teams had been working since early morning to clear drainage lines and drain the accumulated water.
The city corporation apologised for the temporary inconvenience and urged residents to remain patient and cooperate while efforts were under way to restore normal conditions.

item.title: Four KU students sued over NWU student’s death in Khulna
item.description:
A murder case has been filed against four students of Khulna University (KU) and 20-25 other unidentified people over the death of North Western University (NWU) student Md Azmal Hossain in Khulna.
Qutb Uddin, father of the victim, filed the case with Harintana Police Station around 10:00pm on Saturday, said its Officer-in-Charge Md Iqbal Hossain.
However, the names of the four KU students could not be known immediately.
According to the case statement, Azmal was beaten at a mess on Masjid Goli of Islamnagar Road, opposite the Khan Jahan Ali Hall of KU, after being accused of theft on Friday night. At one stage, he fell from the roof of the four-storey building.
He was taken to Khulna Medical College Hospital in critical condition around 1:30am on Saturday, where he died.
Police and local sources said Azmal, a first-year student of the English Department at NWU situated at Sonadanga, ate at the mess on Friday night without paying for the meal, which allegedly led to an altercation.
Several students of the mess and some locals later accused him of theft and allegedly beat him.
He was subsequently taken to the rooftop, where he was allegedly beaten further. His hair was also cut.
Azmal hailed from Bara Sholua village under Darshana Police Station in Chuadanga and lived in a rented mess in the Masjid Goli area near KU.
Azmal’s family also alleged that someone called them during the incident and demanded Tk 100,000. The phone was later found to be switched off. Police said they were investigating the allegation.
“We are investigating the incident and will take legal action against those found to be involved,” said OC Iqbal Hossain.
He said four KU students were named in the case, while another 20-25 unidentified people were also accused.

item.title: Three people, including freedom fighter, killed in Gopalganj road crashes
item.description:
Three people, including a freedom fighter, killed in separate bus crashes in Kashiani upazila of Gopalganj on late Saturday night and Sunday.
The first accident occurred in the Panchabatti area of the Dhaka-Khulna highway.
The deceased were identified as Omar Mir, 75, a freedom fighter and Jahid Molla, 50, both residents of the area.
Locals said Omar and Jahid were walking along the highway when a bus hit them, leaving both critically injured. Omar was rushed to Muksudpur Upazila Health Complex, where doctors declared him dead. Jahid died at the scene.
Sub Inspector Obaidul Kazi of Bhanga Highway Police Station confirmed the deaths. He said police visited the scene, prepared inquest reports and handed over the bodies to the families after completing legal procedures.
In another accident on the same highway early Sunday, a human hauler driver was killed after an unidentified bus rammed the vehicle in the Fokra bus stand area of Kashiani around 4am.
The impact crushed the human haular, killing the driver on the spot.
Rokonuzzaman, officer-in-charge of Bhatiapara Highway Police Station, confirmed the incident and said police recovered the body and sent it to a hospital morgue for autopsy.
The identities of the driver and the bus involved could not immediately be ascertained as the accident occurred before dawn. Police are working to identify the deceased and locate the bus.

item.title: Students withdraw Dhaka-Chittagong highway blockade
item.description:
Students of Comilla University and other educational institutions have withdrawn their blockade of the Dhaka-Chittagong highway after announcing a four-point list of demands, with traffic movement gradually returning to normal.
The students began the blockade in the Kotbari area of Comilla on Sunday afternoon, demanding justice for the murder of 13-year-old Ishayat Shahriar Opratim.
They cleared the highway around 12:30pm after holding a protest procession from the university’s main gate following Opratim’s namaz-e-janaza on campus.
The procession moved towards the Kotbari intersection, where the students blocked the Dhaka-Chittagong highway.
Their four demands are: the arrest of those involved in Opratim’s murder within 12 hours and a guarantee of a speedy trial; an acknowledgement of failure in handling the murder case from the Comilla superintendent of police and the police forces of Kotwali Model Police Station and Sadar Dakshin Police Station; the establishment of a permanent police outpost in the university area; and visible measures to improve the law and order situation in Comilla.

item.title: Call to halt NCT lease process to DP World
item.description:
Chattogram Bandar Rakkha Parishad has demanded that the government halt the ongoing process to lease the New Mooring Container Terminal (NCT) at Chittagong Port to foreign operator DP World.
At a press conference organised at the Chittagong Press Club on yesterday, the parishad gave the government two days to meet its four-point demands, warning of a series of protest programs otherwise.
The demands include scrapping the lease process, withdrawing cases filed against port leaders and 15 employees over previous protests, removing port officials involved in the proposed agreement with DP World, and filling vacant posts at the port.
Joint Coordinator Humayun Kabir alleged that successive governments had attempted to hand over NCT to DP World since 2017, despite concerns over national interests. He said the interim government also continued the process after August 5, 2024, but later stepped back following protests by the parishad, labour organisations and professionals.
The parishad also rejected claims by the port chairman that NCT’s equipment was outdated and operating at only 70% capacity. It said port documents, equipment procurement records and assessments by maritime logistics experts did not support the claim.
It also warned that leasing NCT to DP World could create economic and security risks, including job losses and increased pressure on foreign exchange. It claimed NCT generated about Tk4,500 crore in revenue in the 2025-26 fiscal year, including Tk2,500 crore in net income.
The parishad announced a human chain on September 22 and a protest procession on September 27 if its demands are not met.

item.title: Gopalganj achieves Boro procurement target
item.description:
Gopalganj has achieved its target for paddy and rice procurement under the government’s Boro-2026 procurement programme, with paddy collection already completed and rice procurement continuing for mills that received additional allocations.
Gopalganj District Food Controller Anik Pal Ontu said the Ministry of Food had set a target of procuring 14,583 tonnes of paddy, 14,076 tonnes of parboiled rice and 242 tonnes of atap rice from six government food warehouses in the district.
The government fixed the procurement price at Tk 36 per kilogram for paddy and Tk 49 per kilogram for rice.
“We started the procurement campaign in May and completed paddy procurement well ahead of the deadline,” Anik Pal said.
So far, 14,318 tonnes of rice, including parboiled and atap rice, have been procured. Additional allocations were later given to some rice mills following applications from mill owners, and procurement from those mills is still continuing, he said.
The six government warehouses in Gopalganj have a combined storage capacity of 14,950 tonnes after a 30 per cent increase in capacity. Against this, the district has already procured 28,901 tonnes of paddy and rice—14,311 tonnes more than the warehouses can accommodate.
The additional stocks have been transported to government warehouses with available capacity in Faridpur, Rajbari, the Narayanganj silo, the Mongla silo and other locations, the district food controller said.
Paddy was procured directly from farmers, with each farmer allowed to sell up to three tonnes at Tk 36 per kilogram. Payments were made directly to farmers’ bank accounts.
“ We did not allow any syndicate to become active in the paddy procurement process,” Anik Pal said.
However, farmers and agricultural officials said government procurement covers only a small portion of the district’s total production.
According to the Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE), Boro rice was cultivated on 82,593 hectares in Gopalganj this year, slightly above the target of 82,588 hectares.
The district’s production target was 635,927 tonnes, but actual production reached 646,703 tonnes—10,776 tonnes above the target.
Sanjay Kumar Kundu, acting deputy director of the DAE’s Gopalganj office, estimated that around 17,000 farmers may be involved in Boro cultivation in the district.
“According to the Directorate General of Food, paddy has been procured from around 5,000 farmers. This needs to be increased. If government procurement is expanded, it will encourage farmers to increase cultivation and production,” he said.
The government procurement price was higher than the prevailing market price, benefiting farmers who were able to sell their produce to government warehouses.
Parimal Biswas, a farmer from Charpara village in Raghunathpur Union, said he sold three tonnes of paddy at Tk 36 per kilogram.
“I am very happy to sell my paddy to the government. If the government continues buying from farmers this way, we will benefit,” he said.
Parimal said he produced 12 tonnes of paddy this year and urged the government to increase the maximum procurement limit from three tonnes to six tonnes per farmer.
But farmer Majed Sardar of Khanarpar village in Kathi Union said he produced 21 tonnes of paddy but could not sell any to the government.
“I was forced to sell my paddy to traders at Tk 1,000 per maund. I am disappointed. I want to sell my paddy to the government, so the procurement allocation in Gopalganj should be increased,” he said.
Md Momin Khan, an assistant professor in the Department of Food Science at Gopalganj Science and Technology University, called for increased government procurement, farmer support and expansion of storage facilities.
Nearly 650,000 tonnes of paddy were produced in Gopalganj this season, while the government’s paddy procurement target was only 14,583 tonnes, he noted.
“The amount procured from farmers is very small compared with total production,” he said.
Momin Khan also called for the construction of more government food warehouses so that larger stocks could be maintained for emergencies.
“More paddy should be procured directly from farmers. At the same time, new government warehouses should be built to increase storage capacity,” he said.
He also urged the authorities to curb the influence of intermediaries and ensure fair prices for farmers, saying stronger procurement and storage capacity would help reinforce food security.

item.title: Titumir: Global financial architecture must create conditions for sustainable development
item.description:
Dr Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir, adviser to the prime minister on the Ministry of Finance and Ministry of Planning, has called for comprehensive reform of the global financial architecture to ensure affordable, predictable and vulnerability-sensitive financing for developing countries.
Speaking at the Leaders' Dialogue on “Leading SDG Action” during the 2026 SDG Moment, convened by the UN Secretary-General at the UN General Assembly Hall in New York, Titumir said, "Our broader vision should be collective and forward-looking: a global financial architecture that does not merely finance development, but creates the conditions in which development can be sustained."
He outlined five priorities for reforming the international financial architecture, particularly for multilateral development banks: shifting from crisis response to anticipating vulnerabilities; giving vulnerable countries a stronger voice in international financial institutions; providing longer-term, lower-cost and predictable finance; aligning international finance with national development strategies through coordinated, multi-year financing; and ensuring flexible transition support and preferential arrangements for LDC-graduating countries, including Bangladesh.
He also highlighted Bangladesh's SDG Village initiative as an integrated, community-led approach to translating the SDGs into tangible improvements at the local level, said a press release of the Permanent Mission of Bangladesh to the United Nations.
The dialogue also featured Teresa Ribera of the European Commission, Aristide M‚d‚nou, Minister of Economy and Finance of Benin, and Beatriz Carles de Arango, Minister for Social Development of Panama.
Sherwin Bryce-Pease of the South African Broadcasting Corporation moderated the discussion.

item.title: Farmgate secret meeting: 12 placed on 3-day remand over suspected militant links
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Saturday placed 12 people, arrested over suspected militant activities during a secret meeting at Tejgaon College Jame Mosque in Farmgate, on three-day remand.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Arifur Rahman passed the order after a hearing on Saturday. Earlier, CTTC Inspector Akhter Morshed, the investigating officer in the case, sought seven days’ remand for each of the accused. Public prosecutor Azizul Haque Didar confirmed the matter.
During the hearing, the prosecution said the accused had allegedly planned to create instability in the country and recruit people to carry out jihad. Their remand was necessary to identify others involved, the prosecution said.
Defence lawyer Masud-ur Rahman opposed the remand plea and sought bail for the accused.
According to the remand application, the Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit learned through intelligence and information technology that several young men had gathered near the Tejgaon Coca-Cola intersection with plans to disrupt public order, spread extremism and carry out a major violent incident.
Police later conducted a raid on May 18 with assistance from Tejgaon and Sher-e-Bangla Nagar police and arrested them.
Police said the arrestees were members of a secret WhatsApp group called “Meetup”, through which they allegedly exchanged extremist messages and communicated on various issues. Investigators alleged that they had gathered to plan subversive activities.
The arrested individuals are Mohammad Shihab Uddin, 32; Marzuk Ahmed, 26; Saifur Rahman Khan, 32; Rashmi Mia, 29; Kamichul Islam, 36; Sajjad Hossain, 22; Afif Ahmed, 20; Mohaiminul Haque, 27; Zauji Chowdhury, 19; Shahadat Hossain, 25; Sakib Ahmed, 26; and Junaid Ahmed, 21.
The CTTC said Shihab Uddin had previously been accused of involvement in extremist activities. A case filed against him under the Anti-Terrorism Act with Palash Police Station in Narsingdi is pending trial. Marzuk Ahmed is also facing a pending case under the Speedy Trial Act with Tejgaon police station.
The investigating officer said the accused needed to be questioned to ensure a proper investigation and uncover the circumstances surrounding the incident.The remand application also sought to recover and examine their mobile phones, SIM cards and other digital evidence, as well as analyse cyber data.
Investigators said they also needed to verify the suspects’ communications on WhatsApp, Facebook, Telegram, Messenger and other social media platforms, identify the alleged planners and accomplices, and trace the sources of funding and financiers of the suspected extremist activities.
The court rejected the bail pleas and granted three days’ remand for each of the 12 accused.

item.title: Saudi capital issues first air raid alert since renewed fighting in Yemen
item.description:
Explosions were heard in Riyadh early Saturday, AFP journalists reported, after Saudi authorities issued their first air raid alert in the capital since fighting returned to neighboring Yemen.
The Houthis have been fighting with Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces since the country’s civil war reignited in July, when the group also declared a maritime blockade on Riyadh and began targeting its ships in the Red Sea.
This is the first time the conflict has reached the capital, further shaking a global economy already rattled by nearly seven months of war between the United States and Iran.
“The area is under a hostile aerial threat,” a message received shortly before 3am (0000 GMT) by residents of the Saudi capital warned, urging them to stay indoors.
AFP journalists then heard two explosions, before the alert was lifted about half an hour later by Saudi Arabia’s civil defense agency.
Saudi Arabia is yet to comment on the threat mentioned in the warnings sent overnight to residents of several regions and has not identified where it originated from.
It comes after Riyadh accused the group of targeting Mecca on Wednesday, denouncing it as a “cowardly terrorist attack” on Islam’s holy city, which welcomes millions of pilgrims each year, both Sunnis and Shias.
The Houthis strongly denied the accusation calling it a “worn-out lie.”
In turn, the group reported dozens of retaliatory strikes carried out daily by Riyadh since their lightning offensive this month to take over the country’s entire Red Sea coast, giving them control over the vital Bab al-Mandab strait.
The war in Yemen broke out in 2014 when the Houthis seized control of the capital Sanaa and other regions, triggering in March 2015 a military intervention led by Saudi Arabia.
The fragile truce reached in 2022 between the warring parties collapsed in July, when the pro-Iranian fighters defied Riyadh’s control of Yemeni airspace by allowing an Iranian aircraft to land in Yemen.
Their recent takeover of the coastline has sparked global concern, with international maritime trade already heavily impacted by Tehran’s closure of the Strait of Hormuz since the start of the Middle East war in late February.
The Houthis, for their part, insist there is no threat to shipping in the sea lane -- except for Saudi ships, from the world’s leading crude exporter.
Figures from maritime tracking firm Kpler showed that Saudi exports via the Bab al-Mandab strait had dropped since July, although five loaded ships had passed through in the last week.
The United States, which according to Axios last week refused to strike the Houthis at Saudi Arabia’s request, approved the sale of 48 F-35 fighter jets to the kingdom on Thursday.
The sale, worth $24.3 billion, is intended to help Riyadh “deter current and future threats,” the US State Department said.
The UN said Friday that the renewed fighting had displaced more than 112,000 people while nearly 3,000 others had fled across the sea to Djibouti, heaping further misery on an already struggling population.

item.title: DSCC plans to produce electricity, gas, compost, diesel from recycled waste
item.description:
Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) Administrator Md Abdus Salam has said plans are underway to recycle waste to produce electricity, gas, compost fertilizer and diesel.
He made the remarks as the chief guest at the inauguration of a “Floating Market in Exchange for Waste” at Swarighat on the Buriganga River in Dhaka on Saturday. The program was jointly organized by Bidyanondo Foundation and DSCC.
Abdus Salam said waste should not simply be viewed as garbage but should instead be converted into a resource.
“We are focusing on how we can quickly generate electricity through waste recycling. We believe we will be able to move to the initial stage in this regard within a few months,” he said.
“Then waste will be transformed into a resource. It will no longer be left scattered everywhere. On the one hand, we need to raise public awareness, and on the other, we need to recycle waste to produce electricity, gas, compost fertilizer and diesel. Our activities in this regard are already underway,” he added.
The DSCC administrator said the Buriganga was once the lifeline of Dhaka, but plastic, polythene and other waste now float in the river.
He said the “Floating Market in Exchange for Waste” initiative had been launched to raise public awareness about preventing river and environmental pollution and to promote the idea of treating waste as a resource.
“We know that all the problems of the Buriganga will not be solved through today’s initiative. But it will send a message to the public that we want to do this and that we need to do it,” he said.
Calling on citizens to come forward to protect the Buriganga, Abdus Salam said people living along both banks of the river and those conducting businesses dependent on it also had a responsibility to act responsibly.
“The Buriganga has reached a point where failure to protect it will leave a bleak future,” he said.
He said initiatives were also being taken to make the Dhaleshwari, Shitalakkhya, Balu and Turag rivers surrounding Dhaka navigable.
“Necessary steps will be taken to restore the river-based transport system that previously connected Dhaka,” he said.
Abdus Salam said under the “Floating Market in Exchange for Waste” initiative, plastic and other waste collected from the river and its banks would be accepted through a designated process.
He said there were plans to gradually expand the initiative to all 75 wards under DSCC.
He added that efforts were underway to launch a pilot project in Kamrangirchar in coordination with Bidyanondo Foundation. The project would explore how waste could be recycled and converted into usable resources.
The DSCC administrator also urged citizens to remain vigilant to prevent dengue.
“Dengue cannot be prevented through city corporation activities alone. Coconut shells, water from air conditioners, stagnant water on rooftops or water accumulating anywhere else must not be allowed to remain. If breeding grounds for mosquitoes can be destroyed, dengue can be prevented to a large extent,” he said.
Speaking as a special guest, Dhaka-7 MP Hamidur Rahman said the initiative primarily aimed to encourage people to collect plastic and other waste lying in and around the river.
“Providing food and essential goods in exchange for waste will raise environmental awareness while also promoting the idea of treating waste as a reusable resource,” he said.
He said the initiative should be continued regularly by involving low-income people living along the river.
“If a designated waste collection point and office are established, it will be possible to collect waste while also meeting the food and essential-goods needs of low-income people,” he added.
Under the “Floating Market in Exchange for Waste” initiative, people can exchange collected waste, after it is weighed, for various essential goods, including rice, lentils, flour, cooking oil, fish, chicken and noodles.

item.title: Dhaka air quality turns ‘unhealthy for sensitive groups’
item.description:
Dhaka ranked 13th among the world’s cities with the worst air quality on Saturday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 121 at 9:02am.
According to the AQI scale, the city's air quality was classified as “unhealthy for sensitive groups”, posing health risks to children, older adults, and people with heart or lung diseases, while the general public is mostly unaffected.
Pakistan’s Lahore, India’s Kolkata and Malaysia’s Kuching occupied the first three spots on list with AQI scores of 179, 171 and 169, respectively.
An AQI reading of 101 to 150 is considered "unhealthy for sensitive groups", while 151 to 200 is classified as "unhealthy". A reading between 201 and 300 is considered "very unhealthy", and anything above 301 is categorized as "hazardous", posing serious health risks.
The AQI provides a daily indication of air quality by measuring the level of pollution and its potential impact on human health.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants — particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2) and ozone.
Dhaka has long faced serious air pollution problems, with air quality generally deteriorating during the winter months and improving during the monsoon season.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution contributes to around 7 million deaths worldwide every year, mainly from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

item.title: Passenger held at Chittagong airport with Tk 1.17 crore worth of gold
item.description:
A passenger was detained at Shah Amanat International Airport in Chittagong on Friday after 534 grams of gold, valued at around Tk 1.17 crore, were recovered from his baggage, officials said.
The recovered gold comprised 106 grams of jewellery, 425 grams of gold bars and three grams of gold paste, said Engineer Mohammad Ibrahim Khalil, public relations officer of Shah Amanat International Airport.
The passenger was identified as Mohammad Hasan Murad, 37, from Noajishpur Union in Raozan upazila of Chittagong.
Murad arrived at the airport about 8:45 am on SalamAir flight OV-401 from Muscat. He was stopped as he was leaving the customs hall after completing the initial baggage screening, after members of the airport’s Directorate General of Forces Intelligence (DGFI), National Security Intelligence (NSI) and customs intelligence units found his movements suspicious.
A subsequent search of his baggage uncovered the gold, which officials said had been concealed inside the luggage using a special method.
According to airport authorities, the concealment had initially prevented the gold from being detected during routine scanning. A separate physical search by intelligence officials later led to its discovery.
The recovered gold was handed over to airport customs authorities, officials said.
Customs intelligence authorities are taking legal action against Murad over his alleged involvement in the transportation of the gold.
Khalil said airport intelligence agencies, customs intelligence, airport customs and airport authorities were continuing coordinated surveillance to prevent gold smuggling and foreign currency trafficking.
Authorities are also maintaining increased scrutiny of passengers and their baggage when suspicious behaviour is detected, he said.

item.title: Dr Zahid stresses sustainable, long-term healthcare development
item.description:
Social Welfare and Women and Children Affairs Minister Dr A Z M Zahid Hossain on Friday stressed the need for developing a long-term and sustainable healthcare system in Bangladesh, keeping in mind the needs of the next 50 years.
"We will not remain forever, but this country and its people will remain. Therefore, we have to develop the healthcare system in a long-term and sustainable manner, considering the needs of the next fifty years," he said while speaking as the chief guest at a program held at the National Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases and Hospital (NICVD) in Sher-e-Bangla Nagar, marking the 'First Open Heart Surgery Day' and the 'Cardiovascular Surgical Conference of NICVD-2026'.
Dr Zahid said ensuring free emergency healthcare services was the responsibility of the state, while the country's overall financial capacity should also be taken into realistic consideration. He recalled with respect the contributions of renowned physicians and specialists who had worked tirelessly to modernize cardiac treatment in Bangladesh.
The minister also expressed gratitude to Japan for providing technical and technological assistance in developing skilled cardiac surgeons during the early stages of cardiac treatment in the country.
He said the prevalence of heart disease, including congenital heart disease, is increasing day by day in Bangladesh. If these diseases cannot be effectively prevented, they could adversely affect the country's productive workforce in the future.
Dr Zahid said the government had already waived taxes on valves and stents used in medical treatment to keep the cost of cardiac care affordable for ordinary people.
He observed that the expansion of modern healthcare facilities in the country had significantly reduced the tendency of people to go abroad for medical treatment. The government has allocated Tk 1.43 lakh crore for social safety-net programmes to reduce the sufferings of ordinary people and ensure their welfare, he said.
The minister also urged affluent members of society to come forward alongside the government in such humanitarian initiatives.

item.title: Two BNP leaders accused of embezzling Tk3.7 lakh from two schools in Natore
item.description:
Two BNP leaders have been accused of embezzling Tk3.7 lakh from two schools in Singra upazila of Natore after allegedly taking the money in the name of developing their village.
The incident reportedly occurred recently in Sukash union, drawing criticism from locals after it came to light.
The accused are Abdus Sobhan Nayan, former joint convener of Sukash Union BNP, and Azmal Hossain, former president of Ward 3 BNP in the union, according to local sources.
School authorities and locals said the money came from the lease of 36 bighas of land belonging to Belowa High School and Belowa Government Primary School.
In June, the two schools leased out the land for one year through open bidding after making a public announcement. The leases generated a total of Tk6,71,625.
On June 24, 21 bighas of land belonging to Belowa High School were leased to local farmers for Tk3,77,250. Four days later, 15 bighas of land belonging to Belowa Government Primary School were leased for Tk2,94,375.
School authorities said the leaseholders handed over the money after the auctions. At the time, the two BNP leaders allegedly told those present that the money would be used for the development of Belowa village.
The leaders allegedly took Tk2 lakh from the primary school's lease proceeds and Tk1.7 lakh from the high school's proceeds.
They later allegedly divided the Tk3.7 lakh between themselves, according to the allegations.
The incident has sparked strong resentment among teachers, students and guardians of the two schools.
Belowa High School Headteacher Anwar Hossain said the two BNP leaders used their influence to take Tk1.7 lakh from the school's land-lease proceeds.
He said he informed the higher authorities immediately after the incident.
Belowa Government Primary School Headteacher Masud Rana declined to comment.
However, at least 10 teachers and employees of the two institutions, speaking on condition of anonymity, confirmed the incident. They said income from leasing school land is used for various development activities of the institutions.
“Nothing like this has happened at either school since its establishment,” they said, calling for intervention by the local MP and the administration.
Former Sukash Union BNP president Akhtaruzzaman and former general secretary Habibur Rahman condemned the alleged incident, saying taking school funds in the name of village development and sharing the money under political influence was “very regrettable.”
They said the incident had triggered anger among the school authorities, local residents and political circles.
Another local BNP leader, Hafizur Rahman, alleged that some former Awami League leaders had joined BNP and were engaging in such activities, damaging the party's image.
However, Abdus Sobhan alias Nayan denied taking any money.
“The school's money is with the people of the village. If you can, publish the news,” he said.
Azmal Hossain claimed that using some school funds for the development of local religious institutions was not wrong. However, he denied having any of the money.
Singra Upazila Nirbahi Officer Abdullah Al Rifat said he was aware of the allegation involving Tk3.7 lakh from the land-lease proceeds of the two schools.
“The concerned individuals have been given one week to return the money. Legal action will be taken afterwards,” he said.

item.title: How climate change worsened Nepal's deadly mountain collapse
item.description:
Nearly 1,400 people have died after a mountain slope collapsed and flash floods swept through the valleys of Nepal and Tibet. More than 5,000 people remain missing.
The collapse was initially thought to have been caused by an earthquake. Now, glaciologists and climate scientists have determined that a complex series of factors led to the disaster, with climate change laying the groundwork several times over: Warming temperatures receded the glacier, thawed permafrost and increased meltwater, destabilizing the slope until it gave way on August 26.
“This was not a single trigger event,” Walter Immerzeel, a mountain hydrologist at Utrecht University in the Netherlands, told journalists on a press call. “The failure occurred at an elevation of about 5150 meters (about 16,896 feet) and there were several processes acting together over time scales of years to decades, rather than one factor acting alone.”
The floods began upstream with a large rock avalanche on the north face of Langtang Lirung. That caused a section of the glacier to collapse at the same time, sending roughly 110 million cubic meters of rock and glacier ice, the size of 44,000 Olympic swimming pools, hurtling downward. That type of rock avalanche is rare, occurring at this size only once every 1,000-10,000 years.
The material fell about 1,400 meters (4,593 feet) from the mountain to the valley floor, picking up debris, water, ice, rock and sediment as it descended. The impact released as much energy as a magnitude 5.2 earthquake. As it crashed into the valley, it also tore up buried glacier ice, adding up to 30 million more cubic meters of debris and water to the flow.
Within about seven minutes, the flood reached Nepal and China's Rasuwagadhi border, 20 kilometers (about 12 miles) downstream, moving at an average speed of 170 kilometers per hour (about 106 miles per hour). The flood continued downstream, traveling 200 kilometers in under seven hours.
It was a complex combination of conditions, exacerbated by climate change, that allowed the slope to collapse in the first place. That's according to researchers with World Weather Attribution, an international collaboration of scientists that looks at the role of climate change in extreme weather and disaster events.
Rising temperatures, due to the burning of fossil fuels, have reshaped this stretch of the Himalayas for decades.
Near the failure site, the glacier's edge had retreated just 75 meters between 1964 and 2000. But between 2010 and 2026, it dramatically accelerated, retreating another 373 meters. That stripped away the ice supporting the rock wall above it.
Permafrost — or permanently frozen ground within the rock — had also started to thaw. That took place between 4,500 and 5,500 meters of elevation, a critical band that's most sensitive to warming. As it thawed, the mountain walls became more and more unstable.
In the immediate run-up to the collapse, conditions were extreme. July and August overall were the warmest on record in the area, with climate change adding about 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) to the region. On August 24 and 25, temperatures ran roughly 2.5 to 2.7 degrees Celsius above the 10-year average. A day before the catastrophe unfolded, the maximum temperature was approximately 7 degrees Celsius above the reference mean.
An unusually snowy October in 2025 likely also played a role, generating more meltwater.
Researchers also believe a 2015 earthquake played a role. That magnitude-7.8 quake triggered an earlier avalanche at Langtang Lirung, which may have weakened the rock mass in the years since, priming the slope for failure.
Researchers also tried to find out whether this was a disaster the region could have prepared for and adapted to. They determined it was uniquely hard to detect, as Nepal's early warning systems are designed for forecastable rainfall-driven floods, not quickly developing, cascading events like this one.
Essentially, this kind of complex threat exceeds the limits of adaptation.
The flood outran Nepal's early warning systems and destroyed several monitoring gauges in its wake. The first mass SMS warning was sent about 38 minutes after the initial collapse, but the flood had already reached the border 7 minutes in.
“When warming destabilizes the roof of the world, no amount of local adaptation can fully shield vulnerable people downstream from this scale of destruction,” Friederike Otto, professor of climate science at Imperial College London, said.
“Without much faster action to transition to zero fossil fuel emissions we will inevitably see more disasters of this scale occurring in the years to come.”

item.title: Trump hails ‘major progress’ in setting up US base in Poland
item.description:
US President Donald Trump announced on Thursday that significant progress had been made toward establishing a US military base in Poland.
“Thanks to the bold leadership of my friend, Karol Nawrocki, President of Poland, major progress is being made toward establishing a US Army base in Poland,” Trump said in a post on Truth Social.
In August, Warsaw revealed that it was in talks with Washington regarding a permanent US military presence in Poland.
“If this happens, the location will be announced very soon. This will be a historic step for our Great US/Polish Alliance,” Trump added in a social media post.
His announcement comes despite his administration’s launch of a formal review of its military presence in Europe. This has raised fears among allies that the US could reduce its military presence there.
Nawrocki, who is a conservative ally of the US president, thanked Trump on X, saying Poland was “ready to continue our efforts to strengthen our defense cooperation.”
He added, “I can assure you that the Polish government will do its utmost to provide the best possible location for the US Army base.”
Meanwhile, Zbigniew Bogucki, the head of the Polish president’s chancellery, called Trump’s announcement “great news for Poland.” He also noted that it came on the 87th anniversary of the Soviet invasion of Poland.
In August, Polish Deputy Defense Minister Pawel Zalewski said his country was discussing with the United States the possibility of establishing a permanent US base on its territory.
“We have already completed the initial stage of the process, not to mention the political will, which was expressed long ago,” Zalewski told the public broadcaster TVP.
Since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Poland has been pushing for a larger allied presence on Nato’s eastern flank.
Nearly 10,000 US soldiers are currently stationed in Poland, a member of both Nato and the EU. However, they are there almost exclusively on a rotational basis.
Poland’s proximity to Ukraine and Russia is a key factor in its security strategy. The country allocates approximately 5% of its gross domestic product to defense spending and has been working to increase the United States’ military presence.
In the meantime, Washington heavily criticized several European countries for refusing to allow US forces to use Nato bases in its war with Iran.

Australia to detain tourists who overstay visa
item.description:
Australia will detain tourists who overstay visas to send a message of deterrence under new rules aimed at reducing levels of migration, a minister said on Friday.
Australia's ruling Labor party has denied it is tightening visa rules in response to the rise of the far-right One Nation, which has become one of the country's most popular parties this year with pledges to drastically slash migration.
Under reforms announced Thursday, Australia will stop family members accompanying students, introduce ballots for working holiday makers and crack down on overstayers.
Assistant Minister for Foreign Affairs Matt Thistlethwaite said on Friday that tourists would be put in immigration detention to reduce the level of visa overstayers, which has risen to 77,000.
"Once the word gets around, 'hey, I overstayed on my tourist visa for a couple of weeks, I got picked up and I spent a couple of weeks in immigration detention, it's not a nice place, I'm going home'. Once that gets around, then we think that obviously that deterrence will ensure that people abide by the conditions," he told broadcaster News24.
People who don't have the right to remain in Australia will face a "consequence" and be removed, he added.
Since 2015, Australia's immigration detention centres have swelled with people with criminal convictions awaiting deportation after a policy change that saw mandatory cancellation of permanent visas for certain criminal offences.
Immigration Minister Tony Burke, announcing the new policy on Thursday, said the government would open 250 beds and add 100 compliance officers to house the visa overstayers in different facilities.
Australian Tourism Industry Council chief executive Erin McLeod said talk of detaining tourists was not good for Australia's image.
"I don't think it does our reputation as a welcoming destination any good and can become quite damaging -- tourism is an important part of the Australian economy," she told AFP.
The council represents thousands of small tourism businesses.
Refugee Council of Australia director of policy Rebecca Eckard said the move raised safety and legal concerns.
"It is being framed as punitive to change behaviour. The use of punitive detention is not permitted under Australia's immigration act," she told AFP.
"There has been a major problem with immigration detention," she added, pointing to concerns raised by the government ombudsman over insufficient staffing and healthcare access.

item.title: US approves sale of 48 F-35 jets to Saudi Arabia
item.description:
The United States has approved a $24.3 billion sale of 48 F-35 stealth warplanes to Saudi Arabia, the State Department said Thursday, the kingdom's latest major arms purchase since the start of the Iran war.
Saudi Arabia has long sought to buy F-35s, but officials from Israel -- currently the only country in the Middle East to operate the jets -- has voiced concern about their sale to Riyadh despite a push for the kingdom to normalize relations.
"The proposed sale will improve Saudi Arabia's capability to deter current and future threats by strengthening its homeland defense, and improving interoperability with US forces," the State Department said in a statement.
It "will also augment Saudi Arabia's operational aircraft and enhance its air-to-air, and air-to-ground self-defense capability," the statement said.
The Saudi embassy in Washington praised the transaction, saying it "reflects the strength and enduring nature" of the relationship with the United States.
It added that the security cooperation between the two countries "has contributed to regional stability, strengthened our collective defense capabilities, and advanced our shared security interests."
Saudi Arabia has been repeatedly targeted with drone and missile strikes by Tehran's forces since the United States and Israel launched their war against Iran in February, and has also been hit by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels.
Yemen's civil war had been dormant for years, but fighting between Houthis and the internationally recognized, Riyadh-backed government reignited in July, with the rebels declaring a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia and targeting its ships in the Red Sea.
Washington has not directly entered the conflict, but a US official said earlier this week that an American military task force is working to enhance intelligence sharing and planning assistance for Saudi forces.
The State Department has notified Congress about the proposed sale, which would require the approval of US lawmakers. It did not provide a time frame for the delivery of the jets.
The F-35 sale "will not alter the military balance in the region," the State Department said, in keeping with longstanding US policy that Israel must have a military edge over potential regional adversaries.
The United States has so far only allowed the sales of F-35s to its closest allies, including a number of European NATO allies and Israel.
Washington kicked NATO member Turkey out of the F-35 program in 2019 because Ankara's purchase of a Russian air defense system sparked fears that Moscow could acquire the plane's technology.
Washington also has concerns about potential Chinese espionage related to the jets.
The New York Times reported this week that US intelligence analysts have raised the possibility that Beijing could acquire F-35 technology through its partnerships with Riyadh.
US Representative Raja Krishnamoorthi, a Democratic member of the House Intelligence Committee, expressed opposition to the sale on those grounds.
It should not go ahead "when our own intelligence community is warning that it could put the crown jewels of American military technology within reach of the Chinese Communist Party," Krishnamoorthi said in a statement.
The F-35 sale is the latest in a series of major arms buys by Saudi Arabia this year.
The State Department announced the approval of a $5 billion sale of more than 10,000 bombs -- including highly destructive 2,000-pound weapons -- to Riyadh earlier in September.
Washington also signed off on the sale of 60 tank engines and related equipment to Saudi Arabia at a cost of $750 million this month, and a $1.96 billion deal in July for the kingdom to buy guidance sections that can convert rockets into precision weapons.

item.title: AI doomsday warnings unlikely to slow IPOs but questions linger
item.description:
Anthropic is expected to beat rival OpenAI to the public markets with a blockbuster IPO later this year despite recent doomsday warnings, but questions remain about their business models and whether regulators should step in.
Concerns about the safety of advanced artificial intelligence models escalated this month after an employee resigned from Anthropic while warning that the industry was "gambling with our lives."
Jacob Coxon, who also previously worked at OpenAI, left Anthropic last week amid a flurry of support from his former colleagues, including one who voiced concern about a small probability that AI could cause humanity's extinction.
Last weekend, Anthropic's own CEO Dario Amodei called for AI development to slow down -- but didn't say anything about the IPO.
The fracas forms a backdrop for highly anticipated initial public offerings from both OpenAI and Anthropic.
It's unclear if, or how, either company will address theoretical doomsday scenarios in securities filings, though.
Companies are required to publicly disclose known business risks to investors prior to an IPO.
Anthropic could submit that document to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) as early as this month.
"Are we to believe that there is something that's extremely dangerous that's hiding inside this company because this person that quit said it, and then it was amplified by a bunch of people" who still work there, All-In podcast co-host Chamath Palihapitiya said last week.
"If it's true... (investors) will demand an enormous discount," said Palihapitiya, a venture capitalist.
Altimeter Capital founder Brad Gerstner, who has shares in both OpenAI and Anthropic, downplayed the concerns this week, arguing that an IPO brings transparency for investors.
"Anthropic will IPO. The market knows how to price risk -- see SpaceX," Gerstner posted on X.
Elon Musk's SpaceX raised a record $85 billion in its June IPO, but its stock has lost around a quarter of its value since peaking at around $202 a share.
"There is huge appetite to invest in the AI leaders," Gerstner added.
How Anthropic's IPO performs will also set the tone for OpenAI's debut next year.
The stakes extend well beyond the two companies themselves, with tech giants including Microsoft, Amazon, Google and Nvidia holding significant stakes in the AI labs.
More broadly, the US economy is increasingly tied to the AI buildout, meaning the success or failure of these IPOs carries weight for the wider economy.
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said this weekend that the company would delay its own IPO until 2027, citing safety concerns. It's an "ill-advised moment," Altman said.
Before the recent headlines over AI safety, Altman and executives at OpenAI had already signaled that they were in no hurry to go public this year.
The ChatGPT maker's dealmaking appears to be running full speed ahead, nonetheless.
OpenAI is in talks with investors about raising a new round of funding with a valuation of at least $1.2 trillion before it goes public, while Anthropic might seek a $2 trillion valuation in an IPO that could happen as early as October, according to various reports.
Leaders inside OpenAI have been concerned about investor skittishness, broad market uncertainty and SpaceX's underwhelming stock performance, according to media reports.
Also weighing on executives' minds is a proposal by both companies to slow down development, given recent incidents involving AI technology going rogue.
OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar dismissed the idea that a slowing of pace in releasing state-of-the-art technology would impact the company's core business and revenue growth.
"Even if we stop today, the amount of intelligence that's available in the world is massive," Friar told CNBC on Tuesday.
Anthropic also pushed back on the idea that being safety-minded would compromise the IPO.
"I would say safety has been the core of who we are from the very beginning," Anthropic's head of policy, Sarah Heck, said at a Politico conference on Wednesday. "Our investors know that. Our customers know that."

The deceased were reportedly passengers of a CNG-run auto-rickshaw.
Authorities could not immediately confirm their identities.
Police and locals said a Dhaka-bound United Paribahan bus first hit a stationary Mahindra vehicle in the Kazir Shimla area around 8:30am and then rammed a passenger-carrying auto-rickshaw. Both vehicles were badly damaged in the collision.
The bus subsequently lost control and overturned on the roadside, leaving at least 10 people injured.
Locals rescued those injured and took them to Trishal Upazila Health Complex, where doctors declared two of them dead.
The other injured were later shifted to Mymensingh Medical College Hospital.
Mansur Ahmed, officer-in-charge of Trishal Police Station, said they recovered the bodies.
Police seized the bus, but its driver and helper fled the scene following the accident, he said.

Athletes 'can't take it any more' as Asian Games issues mount
item.description:
The Asian Games in Japan were on Friday facing more accusations of poor organisation with a world champion gymnast "totally exhausted", the public drafted in to rescue stranded athletes and South Korea lodging a complaint about a Japanese warlord.
The continent's premier sporting spectacle opens in Nagoya and Aichi prefecture on Saturday, but the build-up has been soured by several issues.
That includes a shortage of rooms for the more than 17,000 athletes and officials -- a bigger number than the Olympics.
Some teams have also criticised the quality of the accommodation, including beds that are too short.
To save money there is no athletes' village, organisers instead putting competitors in hotels, temporary cabins and on a cruise ship.
Organisers say the accommodation is safe, cost-effective and comfortable.
Chinese gymnast Zhang Boheng, who won two silver medals at the Paris Olympics and has two world championship titles to his name, said he and some of his team-mates were left waiting for six hours after landing on Wednesday.
"I'm totally exhausted," he said in a video published Thursday and shared widely on Chinese social media.
"I didn't expect that after breakfast at 7:00 am the next time I could eat would be close to 7:00 pm," the 26-year-old said.
He said the wait was caused by registration and paperwork, before heading to the cruise ship where 4,000 Games participants will be housed in Nagoya's port area.
But when they arrived at the ship, he said heavy rain prevented them from boarding.
"A whole day was basically wasted like this," added Zhang.
"In the end we really couldn't take it any more so we decided to book rooms at a hotel to rest."
The video has since been taken down but Chinese state media said that other Chinese athletes also faced travel delays upon arrival.
Beijing's consulate in Nagoya contacted Chinese citizens in the area to give the badminton team lifts after issues with a shuttle bus and a shortage of public transport tickets, Xinhua reported.
Chinese social media users applauded athletes, including table tennis star Sun Yingsha, for stretching and exercising at the airport.
The hashtag "Asian Games absurd" has since been viewed more than 94 million times on Weibo.
India's team had similar delays at the airport.
"There was an issue in getting accreditation for athletes at the airport during immigration. There were long queues with a lot of other nations there," India's chef de mission and Indian Olympic Association (IOA) treasurer Sahdev Yadav told AFP.
"But these things happen and we have got everything sorted.
He added: "These are all teething problems and our focus is now on performance."
- Warlord controversy -
South Korea's Yonhap news agency reported that some of the country's athletes waited at the airport for more than five hours on Thursday.
"We are aware of the situation including reports that athletes have had to wait for hours and we are doing our best to handle it," a Korean Sport and Olympic Committee (KSOC) official told AFP.
Also on Friday, the KSOC said it had filed a complaint with Games organisers for featuring a Japanese warlord at a welcoming ceremony.
The event on Tuesday included a person dressed as Toyotomi Hideyoshi, who led Japan's invasions of Korea in 1592-1598, and the ceremony prompted a backlash in South Korea.
Historical issues are sensitive between South Korea and Japan, with Hideyoshi's invasion a significant episode in Korean history and Korea under Japanese colonial rule from 1910 to 1945.
There was no immediate response from the Olympic Council of Asia or the local organising committee.
